TI Telling academic tales: The role of narrative structure in shaping
   research impact across disciplines
SO JOURNAL OF ENGLISH FOR ACADEMIC PURPOSES
LA English
DT Article
DE Narrative structure; Cross-disciplinary difference; Academic writing;
   Research impact
ID SCIENCE; PUBLICATION; INFORMATION; CITATIONS; STORIES
AB Narrative structure, also known as the shape of stories, refers to the way a story is organized and presented from a semantic progression perspective. In academic writing, high-quality research articles are often metaphorically described as well-told academic stories, as narrative devices can present complex ideas in a clear and engaging manner. However, the role of the narrative structure in academic writing remains underexplored. To address the issue, we examined the narrative structure in research articles and its relationship with citation counts from three dimensions (i.e., speed, volume, and circuitousness) and in different disciplines. The results revealed significant cross-disciplinary differences in the narrative structure of research articles. Specifically, articles in medical and life sciences exhibited the highest levels across all three dimensions, while those in social sciences demonstrated the lowest speed and volume, and articles in applied sciences showed the lowest circuitousness. Furthermore, speed was negatively related to citation counts, whereas both volume and circuitousness were positively related to citation counts, except that volume showed a negative relationship in medical and life sciences. To the best of our knowledge, this study is probably the first cross-disciplinary investigation of the narrative structure in academic writing. Possible explanations for the findings were discussed. Implications for researchers and instructors of academic writing were also provided.

AB OBJECTIVE: Laparoscopy requires bimanual proficiency, yet early trainees demonstrate underdeveloped nondominant hand (NDH) performance. We assessed feasibility and impact of integrating structured NDH training with established laparoscopic curriculum for surgery interns. DESIGN: Prospective, single-institution randomized pilot study. Interns were assigned the standard 4-week curriculum of laparoscopic dominant hand and bimanual tasks (Control) or completed assigned NDH tasks in addition to the standard curriculum (Intervention). Feasibility was determined by assigned task completion, daily standard and NDH-specific self-reported practice time, and improvement in bimanual task performance. Performance was video recorded weekly and assessed by blinded evaluators using MISTELS and GOALS scoring. Cognitive workload during laparoscopic tasks was measured via NASA-TLX. Exploratory analyses were conducted within a Bayesian framework. SETTING: A single academic institution with a surgical simulation training program. PARTICIPANTS: General surgery interns on their 4-week simulation rotation. RESULTS: Eleven general surgery interns (6 intervention, 5 controls; all right-hand dominant) completed the study with 100% task completion and practice log compliance. Both groups improved in bimanual performance and perceived cognitive load. Reduction in cognitive workload during bimanual task performance was greater in the NDH group. Time spent on NDH practice over 4 weeks was associated with improved bimanual performance, independent of time spent on standard curriculum tasks. CONCLUSIONS: Structured NDH training is feasible to implement within an existing curriculum and reduces perceived cognitive workload during bimanual laparoscopic tasks. NDH practice demonstrates a beneficial dose-response relationship with performance, supporting its integration into early laparoscopic training. ( J Surg Ed 83:104103. TI Navigating the "Ideals": A comparative case study of early educators'
   sensemaking of quality in the United States and China
SO TEACHING AND TEACHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
ID EARLY-CHILDHOOD EDUCATION; EARLY CARE; TEACHERS; KINDERGARTEN; CHILDREN;
   POLICY; PLAY
AB The current comparative case study investigated how early childhood educators made sense of quality in a Head Start program serving refugee families in the United States and a Puhui preschool serving children of migrant workers in China. Guided by folk pedagogy and teacher sensemaking theories, data were collected through a review of quality standards, classroom observations, and semi-structured interviews with administrators and teachers. Findings revealed that while quality standards in both countries emphasized child-centeredness, individualized learning, and play-based pedagogy, these ideals were interpreted and enacted very differently across the two settings. Educators' sensemaking was shaped not only by cultural beliefs, but also by local contexts, education systems, and broader societal shifts. These findings highlight the need for a contextually grounded understanding of quality that reflects the lived realities of children, families, and educators. Policies should balance standardization with flexibility so educators can adapt practices to their local contexts.

TI The babelization of reflective practice in initial teacher education
SO TEACHING AND TEACHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Reflective practice; Initial teacher education; Pedagogical
   implementation; Formative processes; Critical reflection
ID PRESERVICE TEACHERS; PROFESSIONAL IDENTITY; QUALITATIVE RESEARCH;
   RETHINKING; INTERVIEW; POWER
AB Reflective practice is widely recognized as essential in initial teacher education; however, systematic evidence concerning the conceptions that underpin and shape its effective pedagogical enactment remains limited. In response, this study examines how diverse actors conceptualize, value, and implement reflective practice within institutional teacher education contexts. A qualitative multiple case study was conducted across three Chilean universities, involving 32 institutional actors, including program heads, practicum coordinators, universitybased and school-based teacher educators, and 23 preservice teachers. Data were collected through individual and group interviews and analyzed using thematic content and multilevel axial analysis. Findings show that, although reflective practice is broadly valued as transformative and improvement-oriented, this consensus masks a structural fragmentation we conceptualize as "babelization." Application-oriented approaches predominate, marginalizing critical perspectives, while instrumental implementations prioritize administrative compliance over sustained reflection. The study repositions reflective practice as a formative object whose transformative potential depends on coherent pedagogical and institutional articulation.

TI Impact of generative AI on higher order thinking skills (HOTS) in higher
   education: a multi-actor analysis
SO THINKING SKILLS AND CREATIVITY
LA English
DT Article
DE Generative artificial intelligence; Higher order thinking skills;
   Creative thinking; Critical thinking; Higher education; Student
   perceptions; Faculty perspectives; Latin America
AB This study examines the perceived influence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) on Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) in higher education through a multi-actor analysis at Universidad de los Andes, Colombia. Using a concurrent mixed-methods approach, we conducted nine semi-structured interviews with academic administrators, twelve focus groups with sixty-five faculty members, and surveyed 529 students. Qualitative data were coded for four HOTS: critical thinking, creative thinking, reasoning, and metacognition. Findings reveal that concerns about creative thinking were the most frequently mentioned (31%), followed by general cognitive skills (25%) and critical thinking (24%), while reasoning (11%) and metacognition (9%) received less attention. Notably, patterns of concern varied significantly across stakeholder groups: students expressed greatest worry about creative thinking (50% of coded entries), fearing loss of creative capacity through AI dependency; faculty showed more balanced concerns and openness to using GenAI as a creativity catalyst; academic administrators prioritized critical thinking (30%) and reasoning (26%), linking these to digital literacy and institutional quality. Results suggest the need for developmental frameworks that consider when and how AI assistance is pedagogically appropriate, multi-level institutional responses addressing divergent stakeholder concerns, and ongoing dialogue about balancing efficiency gains with cognitive development. The research contributes to understanding GenAI's complex, sometimes contradictory impacts on thinking skills in higher education.

TI Educator's Blueprint: Six Tips for Navigating What Emergency Physicians
   Cannot Control
SO AEM EDUCATION AND TRAINING
LA English
DT Article
DE burnout; emergency medicine; medical; moral distress; philosophy;
   professional; psychological; resilience
AB Emergency physicians repeatedly encounter problems that clinical expertise alone cannot resolve, such as a patient with decision-making capacity leaving against advice, a consultant declining to come in, admitted patients boarding for hours, or a family asking for continued resuscitation after the team concludes that it cannot succeed. Residency prepares us well for what we can control but offers little guidance about the rest. Some of these encounters produce moral distress; others are frustrating limitations. This Educator's Blueprint presents six tips to face such situations adapted from Stoicism, Buddhism, and Taoism. Stoicism helps distinguish what can be changed from what cannot. Buddhism helps separate a difficult outcome from professional identity. Taoism helps direct the remaining effort toward action the circumstances can absorb. The tips are designed for use in conferences and reflection groups that many programs already conduct. The article also explains why these traditions were selected and acknowledges important criticisms of their use.

TI My Grandmother Was Not in the Textbook
SO ANTHROPOLOGY & EDUCATION QUARTERLY
LA English
DT Article
DE anthropology of education; cultural memory; curriculum; embodied
   pedagogy; intergenerational knowledge
AB This poem reflects on the quiet forms of knowledge that often remain absent from formal schooling. TI Peer Bullying Victimisation and School Burnout in Adolescents: A Serial
   Mediation Model of the Meaning of School and Academic Grit
SO JOURNAL OF PSYCHOLOGISTS AND COUNSELLORS IN SCHOOLS
LA English
DT Article
DE school burnout; peer bullying victimisation; the meaning of school;
   academic grit
ID STUDENTS
AB School burnout has been increasingly observed among high school students. Although several studies have examined the factors influencing school burnout, the mechanisms through which peer bullying victimisation contributes to students' burnout remain unclear. In particular, the mediating processes underlying the association between peer bullying victimisation and school burnout, as well as the roles of individual and contextual protective factors, are still not well understood. Therefore, this study explored the mediating roles of the meaning of school (perceived value and significance of school) and academic grit (persistent effort towards academic goals) in the relationship between peer bullying victimisation and school burnout. Serial mediation analyses revealed small but significant indirect effects, indicating that the meaning of school and academic grit sequentially mediated the relationship between peer bullying victimisation and school burnout. These findings contribute to the literature on factors associated with school burnout among adolescents.

TI Assess, Adapt and Group: Enhancing Early-Grade Reading Outcomes Through
   Readiness-Based Differentiated Instruction in Ghana
SO JOURNAL OF RESEARCH IN READING
LA English
DT Article
DE differentiated instruction; differentiation by readiness; early-grade
   literacy; Ghana; literacy pedagogy
ID ACHIEVEMENT; CLASSROOM; TEACHERS; PEDAGOGY
AB Background In Ghana, students struggle to acquire foundational literacy skills, prompting the government and international donors to identify more effective pedagogical approaches. This study examines the potential of readiness-based differentiated instruction (DI) in Ghana's multilingual, mixed-ability primary schools.Methods Data include longitudinal reading assessments and surveys from a nationally representative sample of 3559 students and 408 teachers in Grades 2-3 across 198 public primary schools.Results Most teachers in our study do not consistently use readiness-based DI methods despite curricular mandates. TI Early Hands-on Surgical Exposure: Outcomes of a Student-led Surgical
   Externship Program for Preclinical Students
SO JOURNAL OF SURGICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE surgical education; preclerkship; general surgery; medical student;
   medical education; OR shadowing
ID MENTORSHIP; EXPERIENCE; SURGERY
AB OBJECTIVE: Early surgical exposure may potentially influence medical students' decision to pursue a surgical career. At our urban, academic medical school, senior medical students developed a Surgical Externship Program (SEP) to provide first-years with hands-on OR experience. This program is a structured 1-to 2-week immersive experience in which first-year students scrubbed into operations, participated in rounds, and engaged with surgical teams under resident and attending supervision. This study evaluates the SEP's impact on surgical interest, OR confidence, and clinical exposure. SETTING: Academic tertiary care hospital. PARTICIPANTS: First-year medical students. DESIGN: First-year students participated in a 1-or 2week SEP with pre-and postprogram surveys assessing surgical exposure, confidence, career perspectives, and interest. Students tracked procedures and skills via a Patient Encounter Log System (PELS). Data was analyzed via univariate analysis through a paired ttest. RESULTS: A total of 28 first-year medical students participated in the SEP; 10 (36%) in the 1-week spring program and 18 (64%) in the 2-week summer program. One did not complete the postsurvey; thus, their presurvey was discarded for analysis. Most students (89%, n = 25) reported prior OR exposure, with 70.4% (n = 19) having <1 month of experience. Significant improvements were seen across all measures of operative and clinical confidence, including scrubbing in, suturing, and participating in rounds (p < 0.001). Perceptions of surgeons were high at baseline, with average Likert score above 4. Significant improvements were seen in views of surgeon work-life balance (p <0.001) and encouragement of students to pursue a career in surgery (p = 0.011). In the postprogram survey, students reported a strong overall satisfaction (mean Likert score 4.70 & sect; 0.54) and likelihood of recommending the program to classmates (mean Likert score 4.74 & sect; 0.53). PELS data showed a documented 189 encounters by 24 students (median 6.5 encounters per student). This includes abdominal exams (n = 12), peripheral vascular exams (n = 5), staple/suture placement or removal (n = 16), nasogastric tube placement (n = 1), and Foley catheter placement (n = 2). On average, students completed 29.2% of the procedural requirements expected of third-year students during their general surgery clerkships. CONCLUSION: Participation in the SEP was associated with significant improvements in students' confidence, operative exposure, and perceptions of surgery. Although participants entered the program with high baseline surgical interest, early immersive exposure may help reinforce career interest, foster mentorship, and support the recruitment and retention of talented students in general surgery. TI The development of social representations of school and the ideal school
   among French elementary school children
SO SOCIAL PSYCHOLOGY OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Social representations; Elementary school; Ideal school; Developmental
   psychology; Children's perspectives; School experience
ID SELF-DETERMINATION THEORY
AB Despite decades of educational reforms in France, children's perspectives remain largely absent from discussions about school functioning. Drawing on social representations (SRs) theory and a developmental approach, this study investigated how 492 French elementary school children (Grades 1, 3, and 5) represent "school" and the "ideal school" through hierarchical free-association tasks. Structural and lexicographic analyses revealed three main findings. First, representations of school follow a non-linear developmental trajectory. Grade 1 students predominantly evoke concrete activities and foundational learning (e.g., play, read, write), whereas Grade 5 students emphasize relational and institutional aspects (e.g., friends, teacher, learning). Grade 3 shows a transitional profile characterized by a lower proportion of original (hapax) associations and a more convergent, normative representation. Second, representations of the ideal school exhibit a distinct developmental pathway: Grade 1 students mobilize mainly playful and imaginary elements, Grade 3 produces the most original corpus (highest proportion of hapax), and Grade 5 students increasingly refer to pragmatic improvements related to school life and learning conditions (e.g., more recess, shorter days, fewer evaluations). Third, children report talking about school more frequently with their parents than with their peers. Taken together, these findings highlight distinct developmental dynamics in real and ideal school representations and underscore the importance of children's perspectives for understanding how school is construed across the elementary school years.

TI Feasibility of Clean Water Supply in a Tropical City: Case Study of
   Kediri
SO CASE STUDIES IN THE ENVIRONMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE climate resilience; integrated water resources management; urban water
   security; water balance; water source diversification
AB The availability of clean water is fundamental to sustainable urban development, particularly in tropical cities experiencing rapid population growth and increasing water demand. Although previous studies have examined water demand forecasting or raw water availability independently, integrated feasibility assessments remain limited for medium-sized tropical cities. This study evaluated the feasibility of long-term clean water supply in Kediri City, Indonesia, by integrating population projection, water demand forecasting, water balance analysis, and raw water source assessment through 2043. Population projections were developed using arithmetic, geometric, and least-squares methods, while water balance analysis was employed to compare projected demand with existing water availability. The results indicate that the maximum daily water demand will reach 618.52 L s-1 by 2043, substantially exceeding the current production capacity of Tirta Dhaha Regional Drinking Water Company (228 L s-1). Among the evaluated alternatives, the Brantas River demonstrated the greatest potential as a sustainable raw water source owing to its high discharge capacity. Comparative analysis with the Langat, Conchos, Mekong, and Mahaweli river basins further emphasizes the importance of integrated river basin management through institutional coordination, upstream conservation, and adaptive monitoring. These findings provide a scientific basis for diversifying raw water sources and strengthening long-term water supply planning in medium-sized tropical cities facing increasing urbanization and climate crisis, while future studies should incorporate climate and demographic uncertainties.

TI Public Sentiments and Community Responses to the Offshore Disposal of a
   Dead Sperm Whale (Physeter macrocephalus) in Viga, Catanduanes: A
   Thematic Analysis of Facebook Reactions
SO CASE STUDIES IN THE ENVIRONMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE environmental communication; risk communication; social constructionism;
   marine mammal stranding
ID KNOWLEDGE; RISK
AB Marine mammal strandings often generate complex environmental, social, and communicative challenges, particularly when management decisions become subjects of public debate in digital media. This study examined how Facebook users constructed environmental meanings and perceived environmental risks following the offshore disposal of a dead sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) in Viga, Catanduanes, Philippines. Anchored in environmental communication, risk communication, and social constructionist perspectives, the study employed a qualitative descriptive case study using reflexive thematic analysis of 152 Facebook comments posted between April 29 and May 5, 2026. Four interrelated themes emerged: contesting governmental authority and institutional competence; constructing environmental and public health risks through lay ecological knowledge; performing civic trust through digital affirmation of government actions; and interpreting the event through folk-cosmological and symbolic belief systems. The findings demonstrate that environmental risks and institutional legitimacy were actively negotiated through online discourse rather than determined solely by scientific information. Facebook functioned as a participatory communication space where community experiences, cultural values, and environmental knowledge intersected to shape public understanding of the incident. The study contributes to environmental communication scholarship by illustrating how digital public discourse influences environmental governance and highlights the need for transparent, participatory, and culturally responsive risk communication strategies during marine wildlife management and other environmental emergencies in coastal communities.

TI Global Citizenship Education for Peace in Politically Sensitive
   Contexts: Research Integrity, Knowledge Diplomacy and Censorship
SO HIGHER EDUCATION QUARTERLY
LA English
DT Article
DE censorship; global citizenship education; higher education; knowledge
   diplomacy; peace; research integrity
ID ACADEMIC INTEGRITY
AB This paper responds to two politically charged reactions to my scholarship on peace and global citizenship education (GCE): the censorship of a UNESCO Beijing conference presentation in Seoul (August 2025) and a confrontational exchange with a Chinese postgraduate student in New Zealand. Drawing on literature on research integrity, politicisation and the conceptual framework of knowledge diplomacy, I examine how scholarship on conflict-affected societies is reframed through nationalist narratives that equate "neutrality" with silence and erasure. The censored study presents a qualitative comparative analysis of 40 faculty in China/Taiwan, Cyprus, Korea and Somalia/Somaliland, informed by the "local turn" in peacebuilding and postcritical theory. It finds that understandings of peace and GCE are contextually grounded: educators in recognised states foreground sameness, while those in contested contexts foster dialogue across difference. In this paper, I examine the study's contested reception and defend dialogic academic freedom as essential to research integrity and knowledge diplomacy.

TI Children's participation rights: comparative analysis of implementation
   practices in public and private preschools in Ghana
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF CHILD CARE AND EDUCATION POLICY
LA English
DT Article
DE Children's participation rights; Early childhood education; Lundy's
   Model; Ghana; Educator practices
ID QUALITY
AB Children's participation rights (CPR) in early childhood education (ECE) emphasises children's right to express their views and have them considered in decision-making processes, contributing to improved cognitive and socioemotional outcomes. Despite the significance of CPR, its implementation in Ghana's ECE system remains undocumented. The purpose of this study was to investigate and compare how public and private preschool educators in Ghana implement CPR, specifically examining the four elements of Lundy's Model of Child Participation (space, voice, audience, and influence). The study employed a quantitative exploratory cross-sectional design that used a structured questionnaire to collect data from educators (n = 172; public school teachers = 50%). Descriptive statistics (frequencies, means, and standard deviation) were used to summarise participants' demographics and CPR implementation scores, while independent samples t-tests and Pearson chi-square tests compared educators' practices between public and private preschools. Educators demonstrated strong efforts in creating participatory spaces (M = 3.0/4.0) and facilitating children's voices (M = 3.3/4.0). However, lower scores were observed with regard to audience (M = 2.4/4.0) and influence (M = 2.8/4.0). No significant differences emerged between public and private schools, highlighting systemic challenges. While Ghanaian educators prioritise foundational aspects of CPR, transformative participation remains limited. Targeted teacher training and policy reforms are urgently needed to bridge gaps in audience and influence, ensuring children's rights are fully realised in ECE settings.

TI Factors associated with a positive vaccination decision as described by
   vaccine-hesitant parents of pre-school-age children
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF CHILD CARE AND EDUCATION POLICY
LA English
DT Article
DE Vaccine hesitancy; Vaccination; Child; Parents; Inductive content
   analysis
ID DRIVERS
AB Background Relatively few parents refuse all vaccinations for their children, but more and more have doubts and concerns about vaccination, even if their children have been vaccinated according to a vaccination program. This study identifies factors associated with a positive decision to vaccinate among vaccine-hesitant parents of preschool-aged children.Design and methods A descriptive qualitative study. The data were collected through an open-ended questionnaire administered to vaccine-hesitant parents. A total of 26 responses were received from vaccine-hesitant parents of pre-school-age children. Data was analyzed with inductive content analysis and reported using the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) checklist.Results Vaccine-hesitant parents of pre-school-age children experienced those factors promoting a positive vaccination decision related to: (1) vaccine confidence; (2) protecting the child; (3) effectiveness of the vaccination program, and (4) socio-cognitive barriers.Conclusion The results of this study highlight the diversity in presentation of vaccine hesitancy as well as the varied factors associated with the vaccination decision-making process. Health services can apply these findings directly in order to respond appropriately to parents' concerns and improve parents' vaccine confidence.

TI Snapshots of team functioning: development and validation of the team
   member perceptions of instructional change collaborations (TM-PICC)
   survey
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF STEM EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Instructional change; Teams; Surveys; Evaluation; Leadership; Faculty;
   STEM
ID PSYCHOLOGICAL SAFETY; SHARED VISION; PERFORMANCE; SCIENCE; CONFLICT;
   INNOVATION; EDUCATION; CONSTRUCTS; COMMITMENT; LEADERSHIP
AB Background Team-based efforts to improve undergraduate STEM instruction have many potential advantages over individually-focused efforts. Team-based instructional change efforts can address broad student learning challenges across degree plans and/or enable changes to develop and solidify over multiple semesters. Instructional change teams can also function as communities of practice that support individual members' learning about STEM teaching and learning. Yet not all teams are equally successful, and a dysfunctional team can result in perceptions of wasted time, energy, and resources. In our prior work, we used grounded theory to develop a model that describes instructional change team functioning. The model includes key aspects of how teams are set up, how team members collaborate, and the team outcomes.Methods Building on this model, we developed the Team Member Perceptions of Instructional Change Collaborations (TM-PICC) survey and collected pilot data to examine its factor structure and initial validity. The pilot survey was completed by 219 team members across 34 instructional change teams at nine institutions. The survey contained 67 items spanning Team Inputs, Team Processes, Emergent States, and Team Outcomes. In this study, we focus on the Team Processes and Emergent States portions of the instrument and conducted exploratory factor analysis on 39 items representing these constructs.Results Exploratory factor analysis supported a two-factor structure for Team Processes and a three-factor structure for Emergent States. The Team Processes domain was represented by the factors Communication and Decision-Making Clarity and Team Commitment, while the Emergent States domain was represented by Team Cohesion, Psychological Safety, and Shared Vision. All five factors demonstrated strong internal consistency and aligned closely with the underlying theoretical model. The final Team Processes and Emergent States models explained 54% and 65% of the variance, respectively. We also demonstrate the practical application of the TM-PICC survey through an example team report designed to provide actionable feedback to instructional change teams.Conclusion The TM-PICC survey provides a research-informed instrument for evaluating and supporting instructional change teams in undergraduate STEM education. In addition to informing team development and improvement efforts, the survey offers a foundation for future research examining the factors that contribute to successful instructional change collaborations.

TI The use of school labs as extracurricular STEM programmes and their
   effects on STEM career intentions
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF STEM EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Usage analysis; Extracurricular STEM programmes; School labs; STEM
   career intentions; Structural equation model
ID STUDENTS ACHIEVEMENT; INDIVIDUAL INTEREST; SELF-EFFICACY; SCIENCE;
   EXPERIENCES; MOTIVATION; BELIEFS; IMPACT
AB Background Extracurricular science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) programmes are very popular and are actively used by teachers and students. Studies evaluating these initiatives show positive effects on cognitive, affective, and motivational student traits, which in turn can influence career choices in STEM. Based on attendance at such programmes, specifically school labs, we measured students' learning gain, the enjoyment experienced during attendance, the change in interest and self-efficacy beliefs in STEM, and how these factors related to STEM career intentions. To this end, 2605 students who had attended a school lab in Switzerland or in the Principality of Liechtenstein were surveyed with a questionnaire.Results Based on a structural equation model, it could be shown that learning gains and enjoyment of the visit correlated strongly. Furthermore, in the model these two variables did not have a direct effect on STEM career intentions, but an indirect one via the change in self-efficacy beliefs. This shift in beliefs related strongly to STEM career intentions as well as the development in interest in STEM, which was also highly associated with STEM career intentions.Conclusions Overall, we could demonstrate the importance of four direct and indirect factors resulting from attending a school lab that are important influences on the fostering of students' STEM career intentions.

TI Cultural variations in the relationship between school belonging and
   social-emotional skills: a multi-group structural equation modeling
   (SEM) analysis
SO LARGE-SCALE ASSESSMENTS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE School belonging; Social-emotional skills; Self-determination theory;
   Cross-cultural comparisons
ID SELF-DETERMINATION; FIT INDEXES; MOTIVATION; ADOLESCENTS; DIRECTIONS;
   RETHINKING; COMPETENCE; VALUES; NEED
AB Social-emotional skills are crucial for student development yet they decline significantly during secondary education globally, raising questions about effective interventions. While school belonging is theorized to support social-emotional development, its cross-cultural universality remains contested. This study examined associations between school belonging and ten social-emotional skill dimensions across eight cultural regions using PISA 2022 data from 527,255 students in 74 countries. Multi-group structural equation modeling revealed positive associations globally, but substantial cross-cultural variation emerged. Harmony-embeddedness cultures (Latin America, South/Southeast Asia) showed the strongest effects, while autonomy-oriented cultures (Western Europe, English-speaking) and Confucian societies exhibited minimal associations. These findings challenge universal assumptions about belonging interventions, demonstrating that cultural values function as crucial contextual factors that amplify, suppress, or redirect belonging's developmental impact. Results necessitate culturally responsive approaches to social-emotional development rather than one-size-fits-all interventions, highlighting the importance of understanding diverse pathways to human flourishing across cultural contexts.

TI Artificial intelligence in mathematics education: a two-dimensional
   conceptual framework and meta-review
SO ZDM-MATHEMATICS EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Artificial intelligence; Generative AI; ChatGPT; Large language model;
   Mathematics education
AB Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming mathematics education just as it is reshaping many other domains of modern life, creating new opportunities that fundamentally change the way students and teachers work. AI has become an increasingly prominent topic in mathematics education, generating a growing body of systematic reviews. However, the review-level literature remains fragmented across different AI paradigms, system types, and methodological approaches. This meta-review synthesizes existing systematic reviews on AI in mathematics education and provides a conceptually oriented interpretation of how AI is shaping mathematics education. We specifically identify and classify the types of AI present in mathematics education as well as the educational functions it fulfills. To organize the synthesis, we propose a conceptual framework that distinguishes between a technological dimension of AI, referring to major AI paradigms and system types, and a functional dimension, referring to the educational roles AI can serve in mathematics education. Following predefined eligibility criteria, 13 systematic review studies were included. The findings show that review-level research on AI in mathematics education is recent and rapidly expanding. Our review maps several AI technologies and systems, including symbolic AI, machine learning, and generative AI. In functional terms, AI was most often conceptualized as adaptive infrastructure, learning partner, teaching tool, and research tool, with a smaller but emerging role of AI as learning content itself. This meta-review provides a structured synthesis of how AI is represented in mathematics education review literature and offers a conceptual basis for future research and responsible AI integration in the field.

TI Positive School Climate and Underrepresented Groups: A Multilevel Model
   Describing Math Scores in Brazilian High School Graduates
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE mathematics; school climate; Brazil; gender differences; public-private
   schooling
ID ACHIEVEMENT
AB Mathematics ability is considered the underlying "fabric of society". Thus, disentangling specific differences between individual and school-level factors is critical for understanding disparities in mathematics achievement, particularly among underrepresented groups. In this brief report on over 700,000 Brazilian adolescents (ages 18-21), we used a multilevel modeling approach to predict math scores based on a number of individual-level and between-level variables. Our findings show that males still outperform females and that students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds achieve higher scores. Beyond these individual differences and the advantages associated with private school attendance, positive school climate as a school-level factor was also linked to better math scores. Nevertheless, positive climate was more strongly related to math grades for male students attending private schools. Furthermore, positive school climate was more strongly related to math scores for students with higher socioeconomic statuses attending private schools. These findings replicate those of previous literature while also expanding on the multifaceted impact of school-level positive climate. We close by calling for more studies that disentangle differences between underrepresented groups in mathematics.

TI Navigating Dual AI Classrooms: TESOL Teachers' Strategies to Reconcile
   Artificial Intelligence with Academic Integrity
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence; academic integrity; critical thinking; TESOL;
   EAP; qualitative research; pedagogical strategies
AB The rapid emergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools has significantly transformed academic writing practices in higher education. While AI technologies offer potential support for language learners, they also raise concerns regarding academic integrity and the erosion of students' critical thinking, particularly in English for Academic Purposes (EAP) classrooms where writing development and independent reasoning are core learning outcomes. This study explores Saudi TESOL teachers' strategies for balancing AI use with academic integrity and critical thinking in Saudi higher education. Using a qualitative research design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 EAP instructors at four Saudi universities. Data were analysed thematically to identify and interpret patterns of AI use and academic integrity challenges across participants' responses. A tripartite framework integrating sociotechnical systems theory, academic integrity scholarship, and critical thinking pedagogy provides a theoretical lens for understanding teacher-mediated AI integration in TESOL contexts. Thematic findings revealed that teachers hold an optimistic yet cautious view of AI highlighting the critical role of guidance and reflection in AI-mediated environments. They employ an emergent, four-dimensional Connect-Guide-Reflect-Assess (CGRA) pedagogical framework to manage the tension between AI and integrity in language classrooms. They demand a shared responsibility between teachers and institutions through clear and consistent AI policies for curriculum, assessment and faculty professional development. This study contributes empirical, practitioner-generated evidence of how TESOL teachers in the Saudi context navigate AI in EAP classrooms. Grounded in participants' accounts, the proposed CGRA framework offers language educators, curriculum designers, and institutional policymakers a replicable approach for navigating the AI era.

TI Unheard Voices, Unseen Realities: The Inclusion of Rural Voices in
   Australian Education Policy
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE rural education; epistemic justice; education policy; teacher
   preparation; student belonging; student voice; classroom readiness;
   regional; rural and remote education
AB Australian rural education policy has undergone sustained reform, yet persistent gaps in teacher retention and outcomes suggest a fundamental misalignment between policy frameworks and rural realities. This paper argues that the misalignment is not a failure of implementation but of epistemology, and that it undermines policy's claim to authority, that is, its claim to know what it governs. Tracing the policy trajectory across a decade of national teacher education reform, it shows how the "classroom ready" construct, built from metropolitan evidence, cannot recognize rural knowledge. Drawing on Fricker's framework of epistemic injustice and its development by Medina, Dotson and Pohlhaus, it diagnoses two mechanisms of what it terms place-based epistemic exclusion. The first is testimonial injustice: rural practitioners' deep contextual knowledge of what enables teachers to thrive is discounted when policy is formed. The second is hermeneutical injustice: the lived experience of marginalised rural students is barely represented in the research base, a scarcity that marks it as unrecorded rather than unheard. As a conceptual synthesis of three completed studies, the paper identifies a patterned gap in the evidence base rather than a causal relationship between that gap and rural educational outcomes. It proposes principles for an epistemically equitable approach within a federated policy system, arguing that epistemic equity is the condition under which policy's evidentiary claim could be made good.

TI Ontogenic, Microsystemic, and Mesosystemic Factors Associated with
   Father Involvement in Their Preschool-Aged Children's Lives: Paternal
   and Maternal Perspectives
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE father involvement; meta-parenting; co-parenting; parental style;
   bio-ecological and systems theories
AB This study examined Greek fathers' involvement with their preschool-aged children from both fathers' and mothers' perspectives, focusing on how ontogenic, microsystemic, and mesosystemic factors are associated with paternal engagement within Bronfenbrenner's bioecological framework. Participants included 106 mother-father pairs with children aged approximately 38 months. Fathers and mothers completed questionnaires assessing beliefs about the father's role, the frequency and quality of father involvement, parenting style, meta-parenting cognitions, and co-parenting quality. Overall, both parents reported relatively high levels of paternal involvement across the different measures. Mothers tended to assign slightly higher ratings than fathers on the overall Inventory of Father Involvement (IFI) and several of its dimensions; however, statistically significant differences were limited, with attentiveness being the only IFI subscale showing a significant difference between parental reports. Mothers also reported more authoritative parenting and higher levels of meta-parenting, whereas fathers reported slightly higher coparenting quality. Correlational analyses indicated that authoritative parenting, coparenting quality, and parents' perceptions of the father's role were associated with different dimensions of father involvement, while demographic characteristics showed more selective associations. The findings support the conceptualization of father involvement as a multidimensional construct shaped by ontogenic, microsystemic, and mesosystemic factors. They also highlight the value of obtaining information from both mothers and fathers when assessing paternal involvement, as each parent provides complementary perspectives on family functioning. These findings have implications for research, policy, and practice by supporting interventions and family policies that promote positive coparenting, shared caregiving responsibilities, and fathers' active participation in early childhood.

TI Extending Computer Science to AI Literacy: The Case for Data Science
   Education
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence literacy; computer science education; data
   science education; mathematics education; high school data science; AI
   education; interdisciplinary STEM education; teacher preparation
AB As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in schools, workplaces, and everyday digital systems, K-12 computer science education faces a growing question: how should students be taught about AI and prepared to engage with it? AI literacy frameworks emphasize competencies beyond programming and algorithmic thinking, including understanding how AI systems operate, evaluating their outputs, and recognizing their limitations and ethical implications. This article develops a conceptual argument that data science education offers an important pathway for preparing students for AI because many contemporary AI systems are grounded in data. Drawing on literature in AI literacy, computer science education, and data science education, as well as our research on high school data science curricula and implementation in Utah and Virginia, this article examines how data science is emerging across courses, curricula, and state-level initiatives. The analysis highlights variation in instructional emphasis, course placement, student access, and teacher preparation needs. It argues that data science can extend computer science education by creating interdisciplinary, data-centered opportunities for students to encounter computing concepts in applied contexts and develop the foundational understanding needed to engage critically and responsibly with AI.

TI Developing creative reading skills through graphic organizers among
   Saudi EFL learners
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE creative reading skills; EFL students; graphic organizers; instructional
   program; Saudi Arabia
AB Although creative reading is a core higher-order literacy skill, it remains one of the most neglected dimensions of reading pedagogy in English as a foreign language (EFL), and no previous experimental study has examined the effect of systematic graphic organizer instruction on creative reading skills in Saudi higher education. This study addressed that gap by investigating the effect of a graphic organizers-based instructional program on Saudi EFL students' creative reading skills. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 43 male freshmen EFL students at Al-Jouf College of Technology in Saudi Arabia, randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 22) taught through five types of graphic organizers (Venn diagram, Know-Want to Know-Learned [KWL] chart, concept mapping, fishbone diagram, and circle map) over eight weeks, and a control group (n = 21) that received conventional instruction. A validated creative reading skills test measured four sub-skills: originality, flexibility, fluency, and elaboration. One-way analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) revealed a statistically significant difference in favor of the experimental group, F(1, 40) = 43.67, p < .001, with a large effect size (partial eta(2) = .52), indicating that the teaching method accounted for approximately 52% of the variance in adjusted post-test scores; the experimental group's raw gain (10.32 of 26 marks) was double that of the control group (5.14). Multivariate analysis of covariance (MANCOVA) confirmed significant advantages across all four sub-skills, with large effects for flexibility (eta(2) = .28), fluency (eta(2) = .23), and elaboration (eta(2) = .19). These findings indicate that structured, multi-organizer instruction produces practically substantial, not merely statistically significant, gains in the creative reading skills of Saudi EFL college learners. The study contributes a validated, replicable instructional model for EFL teachers, provides curriculum designers with evidence for embedding visual-strategic creative reading tasks in Saudi technical education materials, and identifies gender-inclusive, multi-site, and longitudinal replications as priority directions for future research.

TI Learning interprofessional collaboration: connecting courses for teacher
   students and social education students
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE interprofessional collaboration; interprofessional teamwork; social
   educator training; teacher education; university teaching
AB Preparing teachers and social educators for inclusive practice requires learning environments that reflect the collaborative and interprofessional conditions of contemporary schools. This study explored how collaboration between university educators teaching two graduate-level courses could prepare students for interprofessional teamwork in inclusive schools. Using action research across two cycles, we collected students' and our own reflections on the development and implementation of the collaboration. Findings highlight three key considerations: the importance of creating opportunities for relationship-building, connecting theory to authentic examples of inclusive practice, and providing explicit pedagogical support for learning to collaborate across professional boundaries. The study also revealed how teaching teamwork became a process of learning teamwork for the university educators themselves. We conclude that interprofessional collaboration cannot be assumed to develop through shared activities alone but needs to be deliberately designed, taught, and reflected upon.

TI Enhancing CDIO implementation in engineering education: insights from
   multimodal learning preferences
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE academic progress; CDIO; engineering; gender; learning style; VARK
ID STYLES
AB Introduction This study examines how the CDIO framework (Conceive-Design-Implement-Operate) can be effectively implemented through understanding of multimodal learning preferences in 152 first-year engineering students at a Technical University, Chennai. Methods Fleming's VARK questionnaire was used to identify the learning style preferences and a descriptive cross-sectional analysis was conducted to examine their relationship with academic achievement. Results It was observed that 75% of students preferred multimodal learning, with trimodal and quad-modal learners (M = 1.44-1.92) being associated with higher academic performance than several unimodal and bimodal learners (M = 2.05-3.60). A significant association was found between gender and learning style preferences (Pearson's chi & sup2;(10) = 51.819, p < .001; confirmed by Fisher's Exact Test, Exact p < .001), although gender alone did not predict academic performance (p = .828). However, there was a significant interaction effect between gender and learning style on academic achievement (p < .001). Discussion This study proposes an integrated CDIO-VARK framework that connects curriculum structure with instructional delivery and provides engineering educators with practical strategies for accommodating diverse learning preferences across CDIO phases while supporting students' success regardless of gender.

TI From voluntary submission to reactive antifeminism: the appropriation
   and re-signification of tradwife discourse in manosphere communities
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE critical discourse analysis; education; feminism; hate speech;
   manosphere; social media; tradwives
AB This study examines how manosphere communities appropriate and reframe the tradwife phenomenon to legitimize patriarchal values through narratives of individual freedom and personal choice. Using Critical Discourse Analysis, the study analyzes a corpus of YouTube and TikTok content focused on the Spanish influencer Roro Bueno and the associated audience interactions. The findings identify six recurring discursive strategies: discrediting feminism, validating the male gaze, promoting biological essentialism, endorsing anti-progressive narratives, romanticizing traditional gender roles, and sanctioning women who challenge conservative expectations. The analysis shows how these narratives normalize gender inequality while presenting traditional femininity as voluntary empowerment. Audience participation further amplifies these discourses, highlighting social media as a key space for the reproduction of gender ideologies among young people. The study contributes to research on digital cultures and gender by demonstrating how lifestyle content can function as a vehicle for contemporary antifeminist discourse, underscoring the importance of strengthening critical digital and media literacy within educational contexts.

TI A study of the influence of family capital and educational choice
   willingness of county high school students in China
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE county high school students; educational choice; educational equity;
   family capital; student agency
AB The "revitalization of county high schools" represents a crucial issue in the ongoing reform of basic education in China. The school-running standards, the quality of public education services, and the matter of educational equity in county high schools have garnered increasing attention and been assigned a strategic priority for development. This study, based on a sample of 2,809 county high school students in Province A of China, employed descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multinomial logistic regression to investigate their educational choice willingness. The findings indicate that the influence of family capital on the educational choices of county high school students is "present yet limited", primarily manifested in the choice of institution types. The educational choices of county high school students exhibit gender disparities, school-type differences, and grade-related variations. It is important not to overemphasize the explanatory power of family capital. Instead, it is necessary to move beyond the perspective of "capital determinism" and focus on educational choice as an expression of the subjectivity and development aspirations of county high school students.

TI Associations among self-awareness, perspective taking, prosocial
   behavior, and attitudes toward persons with disabilities among high
   school students without disabilities: differences by inclusive physical
   education participation
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE attitudes toward persons with disabilities; inclusive physical
   education; perspective taking; prosocial behavior; self-awareness
ID EMPATHY; INDIVIDUALS; RECOGNITION; SUPPORT
AB Background The purpose of this study was to examine the relationships among self-awareness, perspective taking, prosocial behavior, and attitudes toward persons with disabilities among high school students without disabilities within the context of inclusive education, and to explore whether participation in inclusive physical education (IPE) classes was associated with differences in these relationships.Methods Survey data were collected from 437 high school students without disabilities. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) and multi-group analysis.Results Self-awareness was positively associated with both prosocial behavior and attitudes toward persons with disabilities, whereas perspective taking was not significantly associated with either variable. Although no statistically significant differences were found in the overall structural model according to participation in IPE classes, relatively positive relationship patterns were observed within the participation group. These findings highlight the importance of social-emotional characteristics and interaction experiences within inclusive educational environments.

TI The impact of metaverse use on media college students' understanding and
   recalling of cultural content: a quasi-experimental study
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE enhanced reality technology; media students; metatut; metaverse;
   spatial; understanding and recalling the cultural content
AB Despite the growing interest in studying metaverse in educational and media contexts, the experimental studies that measure its impact on understanding and recalling cultural content are still limited. Therefore, this study aims to examine changes in media students' understanding and recalling of cultural content following participation in a metaverse-based learning experience, in light of the rapid digital transformations that have imposed new types of immersive and interactive learning environments. The study adopted a quasi-experimental design based on two non-random groups, with the application of a pre-test and a post-test on a sample consisting of one hundred and forty-two students from the media students. The same cultural content was presented to the participants through the Metaverse environment, while the means of accessing it differed between a group that used virtual reality (VR) headset and a group that used a mobile phone. The differences were also studied in light of the gender variable. The achievement test consisted of nine content-related items; five items were allocated to measure recalling, and four items to measure understanding. To analyze the data, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used to compare the pre- and post-tests, and the Mann-Whitney test to compare independent groups, along with gain score analysis and covariance analysis to adjust for pre-test differences, with effect sizes being calculated. The results showed a statistically significant improvement between the pre- and post-tests in both recalling and understanding, with large effect sizes that warrant careful interpretation. Furthermore, the post-test scores and achievement scores were higher for the virtual reality group compared to the mobile phone group, and this difference remained significant even after adjusting for pre-test performance. The gender variable had no effect on recalling, while a difference in understanding was observed, favoring the female students. The study recommends employing metaverse environments in teaching cultural and media content and conducting follow-up studies on larger samples and other learning variables.

TI Beyond andragogy: postgraduate students' experiences of self-determined
   learning in higher education: a heutagogical perspective
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE andragogy; Ghana; heutagogy; higher education; interpretative
   phenomenological analysis; postgraduate education; self-determined
   learning
AB Introduction Although heutagogy is widely advocated for postgraduate education, students' actual practices of self-determined learning in higher education institutions remain little explored, particularly in African settings. This study examined the lived experiences of postgraduate students, what enables and constrains those experiences, and how they relate to andragogical assumptions, using the conceptual lens of heutagogy.Methods An interpretive phenomenological design was used. Nine postgraduate students from the University of Business and Integrated Development Studies and other public universities in Ghana were purposively selected as information-rich cases: learners already demonstrably engaged in autonomous, self-directed, or self-determined practice. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews, four-week reflective journals, and learning artefacts, and analysed using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis. Triangulation, member checks, audit trails and reflexive journaling supported credibility, dependability, confirmability and transferability.Results Five group experiential themes emerged: becoming the author of one's own learning; redefining the destination rather than the route; inhabiting two curricula (the visible syllabus and a parallel learning track); the fragility of agency; and crossing the Heutagogical threshold. Participants described a reorientation of learner identity, authorship of learning goals, a parallel learning track supported by digital tools and peer networks, and contextual pivoting of academic content toward the communities they served.Discussion Among these information-rich cases, practices exceeded andragogical assumptions: participants authored their own goals, reflected on disciplinary assumptions, learned in parallel, pivoted in context, and cultivated capability rather than competency. Rather than a linear movement beyond andragogy, however, the accounts reveal an oscillation between andragogical scaffolding and Heutagogical authorship, conditioned by confidence, supervisory stances, workload, family responsibilities, and access to resources. Self-determined learning emerged less because institutions supported it than because participants constructed alternative learning ecologies alongside, beyond, and sometimes in partial resistance to formal curricular structures. Given the small, single-country, largely single-institution sample of already-disposed learners, the findings are interpretive claims about information-rich cases rather than generalisations about postgraduate students. The study contributes to the heutagogy literature from an African higher education context and has implications for postgraduate curriculum design, supervisor practice, and institutional recognition of self-determined learning.

TI Lab-Tec@Home and perceived complex thinking: gender-related patterns
   among engineering students
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE complex thinking; control engineering; future of education, gender gap;
   professional education; educational innovation; higher education
ID BOX PLOT
AB Introduction Lab-Tec@Home combines low-cost control-engineering kits with MATLAB/Simulink (R) to support hands-on experimentation outside the institutional laboratory. This study examined changes in engineering students' self-perceived complex thinking after participation in Lab-Tec@Home and whether the magnitude of change differed between women and men. Complex thinking was conceptualized as a macro-competency comprising systemic, scientific, critical, and innovative thinking.Methods The eComplexity instrument was administered before and after the intervention to 121 undergraduate Mechatronics Engineering students with matched longitudinal records. Analyses included descriptive statistics, paired-samples tests, comparisons of change scores between gender groups, linear regression models adjusted for academic cohort, and exploratory principal component analysis.Results Post-test means were descriptively higher than pre-test means in both groups. Although some within-group improvements were observed, the magnitude of change did not differ significantly between women and men. These findings support a cautious interpretation of the intervention's potential contribution to complex thinking and highlight the need for larger, more gender-balanced samples and stronger comparative designs.

TI Conceptions of assessment among tertiary vocational education and
   training students across school and workplace settings in China
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE assessment; attitudes and beliefs; invariance testing; vocational
   education and training; workplace
ID FIT INDEXES; HONG-KONG; SELF-REGULATION; ACHIEVEMENT; PURPOSES; MODELS
AB Students' understanding of the purposes and uses of assessment has been measured using the Chinese Students' Conceptions of Assessment (C-SCoA) inventory. The C-SCoA has a hierarchical structure with a single second-order factor (i.e., School Quality) predicting seven subordinate factors. However, previous studies with the C-SCoA have been limited to academic-track students in tertiary institutional settings. Taken together, the results suggest that the C-SCoA is a psychometrically sound instrument for investigating VET students' conceptions of assessment across school and workplace settings.

TI Young learners' negotiation of meaning as task-me diate d reconstruction
   across traditional and digital storytelling
SO LINGUISTICS AND EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Task-based language teaching; Negotiation of meaning; Digital
   storytelling; Task modalities; Early childhood education
ID EFL; ACQUISITION; REPETITION; GRAMMAR; CLIL
AB Negotiation of meaning (NoM) is central to task-based language teaching (TBLT), yet studies of young learners often report strategy frequencies without examining how negotiation unfolds and reorganizes the activity in which it occurs. This study examines NoM across eleven storytelling sessions designed in alignment with TBLT and Developmentally Appropriate Practice (DAP), with ten second-grade children and four parent facilitators. Analysis of audio and video recordings, artifacts, and field notes proceeded in two connected stages, combining deductive coding of established NoM strategies with sequence-based analysis of task demand, local trigger, uptake, reconstruction, and consequence. Children drew on a stable repertoire of strategies across both phases, yet the same moves varied in interactional consequence with task modality. In traditional storytelling, negotiation made narrative meaning, form, and the legitimacy of a contribution publicly accountable in talk that then dissolved. In digital storytelling, the same moves settled how meanings could be built in materials and fixed them in a durable artifact, where coherence and authorship became open to negotiation. Building on the established account of NoM as communicative repair, the study broadens the analytic scope to what negotiation reorganizes within the activity, an emphasis captured by treating NoM as task-mediated reconstruction, with task modality bearing on what children negotiate and what their negotiation leaves behind. TI Immersion and Growth: A Study on the Influence Mechanism of Research
   Atmosphere on Graduate Student Competence Development
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE Research atmosphere; Graduate student competence development; Learning
   engagement; Academic interest; Mediating effect; Moderating effect
ID LEARNING-ENVIRONMENT; INTERPERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS; ENGAGEMENT;
   ACHIEVEMENT; PERCEPTIONS; CREATIVITY; OUTCOMES; FIELD; MODEL
AB Research atmosphere is a critical environmental factor shaping graduate students' competence development. Although prior studies have examined graduate training environments, less is known about how research atmosphere is translated into competence development through students' engagement and motivation. Using survey data from 18,715 graduate students at a "Double First-Class" university in China, this study tested a moderated mediation model with PROCESS Models 4 and 7 and bias-corrected bootstrapping. The findings reveal that research atmosphere has a significant positive impact on graduate student competence development (beta = 0.6722, p < 0.001), with learning engagement serving as a partial mediator (mediation rate = 62.19%). Furthermore, academic interest positively moderates the relationship between research atmosphere and learning engagement (beta = 0.0447, p < 0.001). These findings underscore the importance of optimizing the research atmosphere, stimulating learning engagement, and cultivating academic interest, thereby providing empirical support for improving the quality of graduate education and fostering innovative talent.

LA English

DE Burnout; Pharmacy education; Depression; Anxiety; Well-being
ID MEDICAL-STUDENTS; DEPRESSION; RESILIENCE
AB Objective: To characterize burnout and mental health symptoms among pharmacy students, faculty, and staff and examine the associations between mental health symptoms and burnout within a single educational setting. Methods: A repeated cross-sectional survey was conducted at a single college of pharmacy. Students, faculty, and staff were invited to participate at 4 time points. TI Bridging the domain gap for VLMs: A scientific fine-tuning framework for
   precision and pedagogy in astronomical image understanding
SO COMPUTERS AND EDUCATION: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
LA English
DT Article
DE Generative AI; Space education; Large language model; Fine-tuning; LoRA;
   Vision-language models (VLMs)
AB Vision-language models (VLMs) hold significant potential for educational applications; however, existing research has predominantly relied on the direct invocation of general-purpose architectures, lacking systematic fine-tuning methodologies tailored to discipline-specific visual corpora. This study situates its investigation within the context of space education to explore domain adaptation pathways for multimodal foundation models. A high-quality dataset comprising 9838 astronomical images accompanied by structured educational texts was constructed: images were sourced from authoritative aerospace platforms and processed through data augmentation; texts were generated via the DeepSeek API within a multi-theoretical educational framework, yielding a four-level hierarchical structure encompassing Description, Explanation, Connection, and Extension. Building upon this dataset, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) was employed to conduct parameter-efficient finetuning of the Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct model. Experimental results demonstrate that the fine-tuned model achieved a substantial improvement in overall test set accuracy from 62.2% to 91.3%, with accuracy on chromatically perturbed and rotation-transformed images reaching 93.1% and 89.4% respectively, evidencing robust visual generalization. Further evaluation indicates that the fine-tuned model outperformed the baseline in 94.4% of assessed samples. A pilot study conducted with 156 seventh-grade students further demonstrated that the finetuned model achieved high levels of perceived usability, image recognition accuracy, and learning utility, with positive response rates exceeding 86% across all three dimensions. These findings demonstrate that domain adaptation grounded in pedagogically structured corpora enables models to transcend surface-level visual description, generating explanatory text that is simultaneously disciplinarily precise and pedagogically intentional, thereby providing methodological reference and empirical evidence for advancing AI in education from merely "useable" toward being "trustworthy" and "teachable."

   in adolescence
SO EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH REVIEW
LA English
DT Article
DE School belonging; Adolescence; Depression; Suicidality; Suicide
   attempts; Suicidal ideation
ID MENTAL-HEALTH; ACADEMIC MOTIVATION; SEXUAL ORIENTATION;
   SECONDARY-SCHOOLS; SELF-COMPASSION; SUBSTANCE USE; CONNECTEDNESS;
   SYMPTOMS; PEER; IDEATION
AB School belonging is a multidimensional concept of school climate, that describes how students feel they are supported and accepted within the school environment. Studies have shown that students who lack a sense of belonging to their school are more likely to suffer from emotional distress and mental health issues, such as depression and suicidality. Although there is a wealth of research that supports the protective role of school belonging in the successful psychosocial adjustment of adolescents, the findings have yet to the synthesized, due to inconsistent operationalization of school belonging. Accordingly, this meta-analytic study investigates the literature exploring associations between school belonging, depression, and suicidality (i.e., suicidal ideation and suicide attempts) in adolescent students (10-19 years of age) using a random effects model. Results, including 32 studies, support that greater school belonging is associated with reduced reports of suicidality (r = -.248) and depression (r = -.383). In subgroup analyses, these associations were also found to be consistent for gender and sexual minority students, and across all stages of adolescence. Overall, findings support the need to foster a sense of school belonging among adolescents and provide important implications for intervention efforts in schools.

AB This study examines how rapid college expansion in Taiwan has reshaped individuals' subjective social status (SSS). TI Digital access and secondary school completion: Global evidence
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE Digital inclusion; Human capital; Mobile connectivity; School
   completion; System GMM; Quantile regression
ID DEVELOPING-COUNTRIES
AB This study examines the relationship between digital inclusion and human capital development, proxied by lower secondary school completion rates, across a global panel of up to 173 countries (2000-2023). While information and communication technologies are viewed as catalysts for development, empirical evidence on their association with education is mixed. The study distinguishes between broadband internet use and mobile connectivity. It uses a combination of fixed effects, dynamic System GMM specification, and Method of Moments Quantile Regression to examine persistence and distributional heterogeneity in education outcomes. Mobile subscriptions are positively associated with school completion in the fixed effects (beta = 4.34, p < 0.01) and quantile specifications (beta = 3.51-4.80, p < 0.01) but not statistically significant in the dynamic System GMM model. Internet usage is not statistically significant in all specifications. In the System GMM specification, the lagged dependent variable is highly significant (beta = 0.94), indicating strong persistence in educational attainment. Quantile regression results indicate heterogeneity across the distribution of educational outcomes. Mobile connectivity is more strongly associated with completion rates in lower-performing countries (Q25: beta = 4.80, p < 0.01) than in higher-performing countries (Q75: beta = 3.5, p < 0.01), while internet usage remains statistically insignificant across quantiles. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between digital access and secondary school completion is not uniform across estimation strategies or across the distribution of educational attainment. The study limitations are discussed alongside targeted implications for policy and future scholarship.

AB In this research-into-practice paper, we examined how 14 postgraduate EAP student teachers in Hong Kong engaged with generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools to develop teaching materials during a professional practice course. TI Epistemic emotions and participatory mathematical identity in a playful

SO JOURNAL OF MATHEMATICAL BEHAVIOR
LA English
DT Article
DE Mathematics education; Epistemic emotions; Participatory identity;

AB The purpose of this study is to understand how elementary school children make sense of their mathematical experiences in the context of a playful Math Fair, and how epistemic emotions, forms of agency, and perceptions of participatory mathematical identity emerge in these interpretations. An interpretive qualitative approach was employed with 80 students aged 8-11 from urban and rural schools in the Valparaiso Region. Data collection was conducted through stimulated recall using photographs taken during the activity, interviews, and field notes. The analysis, conducted using open and axial coding, identified two central and interrelated dimensions: (a) epistemic emotions-surprise, curiosity, productive confusion, and enjoyment-associated with processes of seeking explanations, exploring alternatives, reviewing errors, and sustained participation; and (b) agency and participatory mathematical identity, expressed in perceptions of competence, legitimate participation, boldness in proposing ideas, collaboration, and peer leadership. The findings show that playful-mathematical experiences provided affective, bodily, and relational conditions for students to explore strategies, review errors, justify decisions, and construct situated mathematical meanings. Implications for the design of school experiences that integrate play, emotion, child participation, and meaningful mathematical activity are discussed.

AB OBJECTIVE: In robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) training, console mediated control of the instruments and operative field, spatial configuration, and different systems change the training dynamics between trainers and trainees. Consequently, RAS changes the entrustment process or how operative autonomy is given and taken in surgical training. This study aims to examine entrustment in RAS training within a national training framework across multiple institutions, specialties, and factors within and beyond intraoperative interactions. DESIGN: We conducted semi-structured interviews and analyzed the data using reflexive thematic analysis. SETTING: Participants included 12 trainers practicing at five teaching hospitals and 8 trainees rotating their training through different hospitals every six months or a year. At the end, trainer and trainee debriefed and planned for future entrustment. Gender was also reported to play a role in the entrustment process. CONCLUSIONS: We provide a roadmap of the entrustment process that trainers and trainees use to give and take the operative autonomy till trainees become independent in RAS training.    Skills Training
SO JOURNAL OF SURGICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE mentoring; surgical education; technical skills; faculty development;
   simulation
ID PROGRAMS
AB OBJECTIVE: To clarify the role of mentoring in surgical training by presenting the concept of the surgical Sensei as a practical framework for understanding how surgeons develop technical expertise, professional judgement, and interpersonal practice. DESIGN: Conceptual article drawing on mentoring literature, surgical education scholarship, and selected concepts from martial traditions. The article frames mentoring as embedded in the everyday work of becoming a surgeon, rather than as an optional support activity. SETTING: Surgical learning environments, including operating theatres, wards, clinics, and skills laboratories. PARTICIPANTS: Surgical trainees, surgical trainers, faculty developers, and programme leaders involved in technical skills education and professional development. RESULTS: The article argues that surgical expertise is transmitted through sustained attention to fundamentals, micro-deconstruction of techniques, and disciplined awareness of the learner, the task, and the environment. CONCLUSIONS: Mentoring behaviors, like technical skills, can and should be practised away from patients in low-cost skills environments. Making mentoring explicit, teachable, and integrated into technical skills training may help surgical educators better support learners' development. ( J Surg Ed 83:104123. ID OPERATING-ROOM; PROGRAM
AB OBJECTIVE: We explored the frequency of narrative feedback within Entrustable Professional Activity (EPA) evaluations for how often narrative feedback occurs, the content of the narrative feedback, and whether the feedback is actionable. DESIGN: Deidentified EPA evaluations were analyzed for inclusion of narrative feedback. The inclusion of narrative feedback was assessed for clinical setting and resident PGY level. A combined inductive and deductive qualitative coding approach was used to evaluate the content of the narrative feedback and determine if the feedback was actionable. AB This study examined how preservice teachers' AI-related knowledge relates to AI reliance and attitudes toward AI use in academic work. Using a cross-sectional correlational design, data from 202 preservice English language teachers at a Turkish state university were analyzed with mediation and moderation models. AB This qualitative case study examines how resilience develops across career stages among Chinese master teachers.
