TI Pharmacological therapy and dietary intervention for obesity management:
   A one-year prospective cohort study in Baghdad
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Anti-obesity agents; counseling; diet therapy; obesity management;
   prospective studies; treatment outcome
ID WEIGHT-LOSS
AB BACKGROUND:Evidence directly comparing long-term pharmacological therapy and structured dietary intervention for obesity in Middle Eastern populations is limited. This study provides 12-month real-world comparative data from specialized obesity clinics in Baghdad, Iraq. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A prospective cohort study included 120 adults with obesity (BMI >= 30 kg/m2) from June 2024 to June 2025. Participants received either pharmacological therapy (orlistat 120 mg three times daily or liraglutide 3.0 mg/day; n = 60) with standard lifestyle advice, or intensive individualized dietary counseling by board-certified dietitians (n = 60). The primary outcome was percentage weight loss at 12 months. Secondary outcomes assessed body composition, metabolic parameters, physical activity, adherence, adverse effects, and quality of life. Between-group differences were analyzed using independent t-tests with exact P values and 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS:At 12 months, pharmacological therapy associated with greater early weight loss but reached a plateau (13.5 +/- 3.7% vs. 11.3 +/- 4.3%, P < 0.001; 95% CI: 1.1-2.8%). Dietary intervention associated with higher fat-mass loss (68.9% vs. 53.1%, P < 0.001), better lean-mass preservation (P = 0.003), and superior improvements in LDL-cholesterol (P = 0.012), fasting glucose (P = 0.047), systolic blood pressure (P = 0.041), and physical activity (P = 0.001). Adherence (73.3% vs. 58.3%, P = 0.038) and patient satisfaction (P < 0.001) were higher with diet, while gastrointestinal side effects were more common with pharmacotherapy (68.3% vs. 11.7%, P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS:Intensive dietary counseling yielded to superior long-term metabolic, behavioral, and patient-centered outcomes with better adherence, supporting its use as a first-line obesity treatment. Pharmacological therapy may be an adjunct for selected patients, highlighting the importance of structured, dietitian-led lifestyle programs within health systems.

TI Relationship between pregnancy risk factors and ABG umbilical cord of
   the infant after birth
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Asphyxia; hypoxia; neonatal; PH; umbilical arterial blood gas
ID BLOOD-GAS-ANALYSIS
AB BACKGROUND: Newborn assessment using Umbilical arterial blood gas (UABG) analysis is more objective than other methods for predicting neonatal outcome. Acidic neonates may be at risk of adverse consequences after birth. This study was conducted to determine the risk factors during pregnancy and their effect on the arterial blood gas (ABG) of the neonates after birth. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted on 1794 mothers hospitalized for termination of pregnancy who were referred to Imam Hossein Medical Training Center in Tehran during the years 2021-2023. Information was collected through a checklist before and after delivery. Also, to perform ABG and VBG, a blood sample was taken from the neonate's umbilical cord and extracted from the file. Data analysis was done using SPSS version 25 statistical software. RESULTS: In this study, between different ABG levels and maternal characteristics, BMI, oligohydramnios, placental abruption, IUGR, acreta, PPROM, delivery mode, and labor with induction, COVID-19, HTN, heart disease, anemia, diabetes, gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia and addiction statistically significant difference was observed (P < 0.05). A significant difference was observed between preterm infants, weighing less than 2500 grams, Apgar score lower than 7 in the first and fifth minutes, and hospitalization in NICU with different levels of ABG PH (P < 0.05). In the multivariable model, fetal distress (OR: 3.51, 95% CI: 1.91-6.44), GDM (Insulin, OR = 5.08; 95% CI: 2.60-9.95), Gestational age at birth (<37, OR = 2.25; 95% CI: 1.23-4.12) were associated with an increased odds of ABG acid level. Also, in the multivariable model, fetal distress (OR: 2.30, 95% CI: 1.70-3.12), GDM (Insulin, OR = 2.48; 95% CI: 1.70-3.64 and diet, OR = 2.42; 95% CI: 1.46-4.02), Labor (Induction, OR = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.10-2), Gestational age at birth (<37, OR = 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.92) were associated with an increased odds of ABG hypoxia level. CONCLUSION: It can be concluded that umbilical cord blood gas is closely related to neonatal prognosis and is a useful tool for screening newborns at risk. ABG should be considered for all deliveries, as it is an accurate screening test for hypoxia and neonatal asphyxia.

TI Optimizing the drug supply chain in hospitals: A mixed-method study in
   Iran
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Healthcare system; hospitals; medicine; monitoring; supply chain
ID ADHERENCE
AB BACKGROUND:The management of the drug supply chain (DSC) is crucial for the success of the healthcare system in ensuring the health of the population. This study aimed to examine the factors affecting the DSC in hospitals across Iran.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This mixed-methods study was conducted in 2024 at a large teaching hospital in Tehran. The study population included hospital administrators and healthcare professionals. The most important criterion for inclusion in the study was having sufficient knowledge and experience. Data were collected using a researcher-developed questionnaire of 28 items across five dimensions. Data analysis was performed using SPSS and AMOS software.RESULTS:A total of 200 individuals participated in the study. The Cronbach's alpha coefficient was calculated to be 0.830. The results of the second-order confirmatory factor analysis showed that the most important factors affecting the DSC are human capital, information technology and intelligence, and financial and physical resources.CONCLUSION:To enhance the efficiency of the DSC and improve health policies, it is essential to invest in targeted training programs for employees to strengthen their skills. Additionally, establishing a transparent database using information technologies, along with implementing warehouse management systems for optimal drug storage, can facilitate access to vital information and significantly improve access to medications.

TI Trends, collaboration, and impact of scientific research on the
   Mediterranean diet during pregnancy
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Bibliometric analysis; diet Mediterranean; pregnancy; woman pregnant
AB BACKGROUND:The Mediterranean diet (MED) is well recognized for its general health benefits and, specifically, during pregnancy, where it may reduce risks such as gestational diabetes, intrauterine growth restriction, preterm birth, and low birth weight. It is also associated with improved maternal metabolic, psychological, and immune outcomes. This study analyzes the scientific production on MED during pregnancy.MATERIALS AND METHODS:descriptive bibliometric study was conducted on original articles addressing MED in pregnant women, published in Scopus (2015-2024). Predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria were applied, selecting 211 documents. We used SciVal and Bibliometrix (RStudio) to estimate production, bibliometric impact, and collaboration network indicators; Bradford's law to identify core journals; and MS Excel for trend analysis.RESULTS:Scientific output has shown sustained growth over the last decade, concentrated in Q1 journals such as Nutrients, American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, and Frontiers in Nutrition. Spain led in volume and impact, with consolidated networks involving institutions such as Harvard University. National co-authorship showed higher average impact than international collaborations. Latin America, Africa, and much of Asia were underrepresented, limiting the global applicability of findings.CONCLUSION:Research on the Mediterranean diet during pregnancy has shown consolidation in both volume and impact, driven by scientific advances and the inclusion of this dietary pattern in clinical guidelines. However, geographic, and thematic gaps remain, requiring more inclusive, multicenter, and population-diverse research agendas to maximize global relevance and applicability.

TI Design, implementation, and evaluation of the effectiveness of a labor
   process application to enhance the confidence and self-efficacy of
   midwifery students
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Midwifery; mobile application; natural childbirth; self-concept;
   self-efficacy
ID EDUCATION; SKILLS
AB BACKGROUND: Attention to the quantitative and qualitative aspects of midwifery education is of great importance. The virtual space can enhance the capabilities of midwifery students during the learning process of labor. The present study aims to design, implement, and evaluate the effectiveness of a labor process application to enhance the confidence and self-efficacy of midwifery students. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study is of a semi-experimental type with a pre-test and post-test design conducted in two phases: In the first phase, the content of the program will be designed and implemented based on the midwifery curriculum (labor process by the Ministry of Health in Iran). In the second phase, the evaluation of the application's effectiveness will be conducted based on the Kirkpatrick model. Students will complete demographic characteristics form before the intervention. The Cooper-Smith Self-Esteem Inventory, Sherer's Self-Efficacy Questionnaire, and Visual Analog Scale Questionnaire will be completed before, immediately after, and 4 weeks after the intervention, along with the teaching satisfaction questionnaire, which will be completed immediately, and 4 weeks after the intervention. To analyze the data, version 26 of SPSS software (IBM Corp, Armonk, NY, USA) will be used, employing descriptive statistics, including minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation for quantitative variables, as well as frequency and percentage for qualitative variables. Additionally, paired t-tests and one-way analysis of variance will be used. The criterion for significance will be based on P < 0.05. CONCLUSION: The study is expected to provide evidence on the effectiveness of digital interventions in midwifery education. If successful, the application could complement traditional training, enhance clinical competence, standardize education, and inform national health policy by supporting integration of innovative digital tools into curricula. Ultimately, this intervention aims to strengthen students' practical skills, improve maternal and neonatal care, and contribute to a competent and responsive maternal health workforce.

TI Web-based clinical training of emergency trolley; new approach for
   nursing students: An interventional study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Cardiopulmonary resuscitation; education; nursing students
ID CARDIOPULMONARY-RESUSCITATION
AB BACKGROUND:Education about cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is imperative for nursing students, and web-based training systems has become increasingly prevalent. The purpose of this study was to investigate effect of web-based training system on the knowledge, satisfaction, and ease of use on nursing students.MATERIALS AND METHODS:The present study was conducted semi-experimentally on 60 undergraduate nursing students, with a convenient sampling approach and random allocation to control and intervention groups by blocking. The intervention was educational web-based application, accessible via QR codes during 8 weeks, and the control group received the same content in the form of lectures by the same lecturer.    students: A cross-sectional survey research in Iraq

LA English
DT Article
DE A cross-sectional survey; factors affecting; nursing students; sleep
   quality
AB BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE:Total sleep duration, onset latency, sleep efficiency, and other factors are frequently used to define the quality of sleep. Sleep disturbances are a prevalent health issue that is predicted to increase and have more significant effects on adults, particularly on medical students, specifically nursing students. Additionally, we have a few studies on sleep quality that we have documented. The objective of the study to determine the factors affecting nursing Students' sleep quality.MATERIALS AND METHODS:The study uses a cross-sectional methodology and an analytical-observational research design. Less than six hours of sleep per day is the norm for students. Additionally, students who abstain from smoking, get more than eight hours of sleep each day, and limit their intake of caffeinated beverages like tea and coffee sleep better.

TI Fatigue, anthropometric profile, and health-related quality of life
   among fifth-year medical students: A single-center cross-sectional study
   from Kazakhstan
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Body mass index; cross-sectional studies; education; exercise; fatigue;
   medical; quality of life; students; undergraduate
ID PSYCHOMETRIC QUALITIES; SEVERITY SCALE
AB BACKGROUND: Fatigue is a familiar problem in medical training, and a growing body of work has linked it to worse academic performance and lower psycho-emotional well-being. Few data are available for Central Asian student cohorts. We set out to measure the prevalence of fatigue in a single fifth-year cohort and to test how it relates to body mass index (BMI), physical activity, and self-reported quality of life (QoL). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Cross-sectional, single-center survey conducted in the middle of the academic semester at a medical faculty in Kazakhstan, on fifth-year students only. Two hundred and sixty-nine fifth-year medical students completed the survey. We measured fatigue with the fatigue assessment scale (FAS) and the fatigue severity scale (FSS), and quality of life with the Dartmouth COOP Functional Health Assessment Charts/World Organization of Family Doctors (COOP-WONCA) charts. Body mass index and physical activity (short international physical activity questionnaire [IPAQ] adaptation) were collected by self-report. Descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), the Chi-square test, and multinomial logistic regression were run in IBM SPSS Statistics 23.0. Two-tailed P < 0.05. RESULTS: Clinically significant fatigue (FSS >= 4) was found in 27.7% of the cohort. The composite COOP-WONCA score split students into three groups (good, moderate, poor quality of life). Physical inactivity was the strongest independent predictor of falling into the poor-QoL group (OR approximate to 3.4-3.6, P < 0.05), while higher FSS scores independently predicted moderate (vs good) QoL (OR = 1.05 per point, P = 0.048). BMI was not an independent predictor. CONCLUSIONS: Roughly 1 in 4 fifth-year medical students reach the clinical threshold for fatigue by mid-semester, and this is associated with measurable losses in daily and social functioning. Activity-level interventions look like the most promising entry point. To our knowledge, this is the first Central Asian study to combine FAS, FSS, and COOP-WONCA in one cohort and use multinomial logistic regression to identify independent predictors of poor QoL in medical students.

TI Studying the effect of implementing the World Health Organization's
   labor and delivery management program on improving mothers' experience
   and satisfaction of childbirth
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Childbirth experience; childbirth satisfaction; labor and delivery
   management program; vaginal delivery
ID NEGATIVE BIRTH EXPERIENCE; STRESS SYMPTOMS; MENTAL-HEALTH; RISK-FACTORS;
   PATIENT; PERCEPTIONS; IMPACT; CARE; POSTPARTUM; PAIN
AB BACKGROUND: The experiences that women gain from the childbirth process are considered as one of the important childbirth outcomes. On the other hand, one of the important factors for deciding on the next pregnancy is the type of experience gained from the previous childbirth. Having a negative experience and dissatisfaction with the previous childbirth reduces the likelihood of deciding to have another pregnancy. Adding woman-centered care, including safe childbirth checklist, can play an important role in satisfaction with childbirth and the childbirth experience. Therefore, this study was conducted to determine the effect of the labor and delivery management program on the experience and satisfaction of vaginal delivery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This clinical trial study was conducted on 940 women (two groups of 470) with gestational age less than 37 weeks, who were hospitalized for vaginal or cesarean delivery in 2022. Twenty-five 1-h sessions were allocated to train care providers by the principal investigator. Within 48 h after delivery, the McKay Childbirth Satisfaction Questionnaire and after at least one month after delivery, the Childbirth Experience Questionnaire, version 2.0, were completed by mothers who had given birth in the intervention and control groups and by research assistants. Finally, the data were analyzed with SPSS software. RESULTS: The results of the independent t-test showed that the level of satisfaction (and its dimensions) was significantly higher in the intervention group (P < 0.001). Also, the results of the independent t-test in the two groups showed that the level of experience (and its subscales) was significantly higher in the intervention group (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: The Labor and Delivery Management Program, using the World Health Organization checklist, was able to increase pregnant mothers' satisfaction with the birth process and create a positive experience for them. Achieving these outcomes increased mothers' desire to have another child.

TI Application of the theory of planned behaviour to assess junk food
   consumption patterns among college students using online food delivery
   apps in India: A cross-sectional study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adolescents; college students; health behavior; junk food; online food
   delivery apps; theory of planned behavior
ID INTENTION
AB BACKGROUND: Junk food, characterized by high caloric value and low nutritional content, poses a growing public health concern, especially among adolescents and young adults. The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) offers a structured framework for understanding health-related behaviors, including dietary choices. This study aimed to evaluate junk food consumption behavior among college students through the lens of TPB, specifically in the context of online food delivery app usage. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 327 college students from various academic disciplines using a multistage random sampling method. A structured, pretested questionnaire comprising 28 items across six TPB domains was used. Data were compiled using Microsoft Excel and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics (v21.0). Descriptive statistics, Chi-square test, Unpaired t-test, and Pearson correlation coefficients were used to explore the relationships between TPB constructs and junk food consumption behavior. RESULTS: Among the participants, 58.1% had a normal BMI. Female students demonstrated higher mean attitude (27.8 +/- 3.93) and perceived behavioral control (PBC) scores (11.96 +/- 3.60) compared with men (attitude: 27.4 +/- 4.6; PBC: 11.4 +/- 3.91). Conversely, men had a higher mean subjective norm score (5.57 +/- 1.87) than women. A significant positive correlation was observed between subjective norms and frequency of ordering junk food (r = 0.165, P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: The findings suggest gender-specific differences in TPB constructs related to junk food consumption. While women showed greater attitude and control toward avoiding unhealthy foods, men were more influenced by social norms. Enhancing perceived behavioral control and addressing peer influences may be effective strategies to reduce junk food intake among college students.

TI Efficacy of new a novel sawdust-plaster material related to improved
   pain reduction and healing among fracture patients: A randomized
   clinical trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Clinical recovery; orthopedic nursing; pain reduction; patient comfort;
   sawdust-plaster mixture
AB BACKGROUND:Acute fractures often require prolonged immobilization, which is frequently associated with significant pain and physical discomfort. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of an innovative birch sawdust-plaster mixture in reducing pain and improving clinical outcomes compared with traditional plaster of Paris.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A single-blind, true experimental design was conducted between May and September 2025 in Baghdad, Iraq. A total of 56 adult patients with upper limb fractures who met the inclusion criteria were recruited and randomly allocated into two groups: the intervention group (n = 27, sawdust-plaster back-slab) and the control group (n = 29, traditional back-slab). Randomization was achieved using sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes. Data were collected using a sociodemographic sheet and the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 30 employing independent t-tests and Chi-square tests to compare outcomes.RESULTS:The intervention group demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in pain scores (25.24 \pm 4.1) compared with the control group (31.53 \pm 5.2; P = 0.039). In addition, the intervention group reported a shorter duration to reach clinical comfort (24.37 days) and a higher prevalence of mild pain levels (77.8%) postintervention. While age influenced pain perception in the intervention group, the primary improvements were attributed to the material's properties.CONCLUSIONS:The sawdust-plaster mixture is significantly more effective than traditional casting in reducing pain and accelerating clinical recovery. To improve patient outcomes, we propose that healthcare facilities integrate this low-cost and sustainable mixture into standard orthopedic protocols. Furthermore, it is recommended that nursing professionals and policy-makers advocate for the use of such eco-friendly materials to enhance patient satisfaction and minimize the physical burden of immobilization.

TI Identifying the requirements for the implementation of teledentistry in
   rural areas: A scoping review protocol
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Dental care; health services accessibility; rural health; teledentistry;
   telemedicine
ID GLOBAL BURDEN
AB Oral health disparities in rural areas of developing countries are exacerbated by geographic barriers, limited infrastructure, and workforce shortages. Teledentistry, a branch of telemedicine, offers a promising solution to improve access to dental care. This scoping review aims to identify the infrastructure, workforce, and patient-related requirements for implementing teledentistry in rural settings. In this scoping review, Arksey and O'Malley's five-stage framework will be used. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase databases will be used to search for studies using a detailed search strategy. Using specified inclusion and exclusion criteria, studies that focus on identifying the challenges of implementing teledentistry in rural areas, and were published between 2004 and 2024, will be identified and reviewed. An interdisciplinary team will develop search strategies, and two researchers will independently review eligible studies for final study selection. Finally, the data will be extracted and categorized to enable statistical analysis of the results. Only English-language studies will be included due to resource constraints. Two independent reviewers will screen and select studies, with data extracted using the MAXQDA 2020 software. This review will map key requirements for teledentistry implementation, guiding policymakers and practitioners in designing effective programs to enhance dental care access in rural areas.

TI Exploring the mediating role of self-compassion in the relationship
   between emotional distress and quality of life in celiac disease
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Anxiety; celiac disease; depression; quality of life; self-compassion
ID GLUTEN-FREE DIET; ADHERENCE; DISORDERS; ADULTS; METAANALYSIS;
   ASSOCIATION; DEPRESSION; SYMPTOMS; ANXIETY; BURDEN
AB BACKGROUND:Celiac disease is a chronic autoimmune condition with gastrointestinal and extraintestinal symptoms, often impairing physical and psychological well-being. Although a strict gluten-free diet remains the only effective treatment, many patients continue to experience persistent, distressing symptoms. Psychological difficulties-particularly anxiety and depression-are highly prevalent among individuals with celiac disease. Self-compassion has been suggested as a positive psychological resource that may influence the impact of anxiety and depression on psychological and social quality of life in this population. This study aimed to investigate whether self-compassion mediates the relationships between anxiety, depression, and the psychological and social dimensions of quality of life in individuals with celiac disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cross-sectional study was conducted with 198 adult celiac patients recruited from Taleghani Hospital in Tehran, Iran. Participants completed validated measures of anxiety, depression, self-compassion, and quality of life. Mediation analyses were performed using the R lavaan package. RESULTS:Self-compassion fully mediated the relationship between anxiety and psychological quality of life (P < 0.001), and partially mediated the relationship between depression and psychological quality of life (P < 0.001). Depression significantly predicted social quality of life, but self-compassion showed no significant mediation for social QoL (P > 0.05). CONCLUSION:Self-compassion mitigates the impact of anxiety and depression on psychological QoL but not social QoL, while depression strongly impairs social functioning. To enhance QoL in celiac disease, self-compassion therapy could be integrated into clinical care to improve psychological well-being, while cognitive-behavioral or group-based interventions should be explored to address depression's social impact more effectively.

TI A study of factors associated with needle stick injuries among
   healthcare workers using structural equation modelling
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE HCW; latent variables; modelling; needle
AB BACKGROUND:Needlestick injuries (NSI) are a major concern in every hospital. Contaminated needles, scalpels, glass sharps, and other sharp objects can expose healthcare workers (HCWs) to blood. There are significant and maybe lethal risks associated with this. OBJECTIVES:To determine the prevalence of NSIs and factors associated with it using structural equation modelling (SEM). MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cross-sectional study was conducted in tertiary care hospital in Lucknow among healthcare workers (HCWs) with minimum one year of working in the hospital. Data were collected about needle stick injuries that happened between April 2023 and March 2024. AMOS-SPSS 22 was used for data analysis, and SEM was used to find correlations between latent variables. RESULT:The prevalence of NSIs was found to be 11.7% among healthcare professionals (25 out of 213) who had needle stick injuries. NSI was found to be statistically significantly associated with healthcare workers' gender, years of experience, manual needle disassembly, and working shift (P < 0.0001). All factors had significant effects on NSI. The positive effects were: gender (0.985), working shift (0.24), dissembling of needle by hand (0.189), and marital status (0.213). The negative effects were: experience (0.737) and age (0.018). CONCLUSION:Larger research can be conducted to confirm the current study's conclusions.

TI Anthropometric profile, hypertension, and lifestyle risk factors: A
   cross-sectional study among Kurdish medical students
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Body mass index; hypertension; lifestyle; medical student;
   noncommunicable diseases; risk factors
ID BODY-MASS INDEX
AB BACKGROUND: Medical students, as future healthcare professionals, should model healthy lifestyle behaviors. However, their own practices and health profiles often fall short of optimal standards. This study assessed anthropometric measures, lifestyle habits, and clinical risk factors for non-communicable diseases among Kurdish medical students. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 280 undergraduate medical students (80 males, 200 females) aged 18-24 years at Hawler Medical University. Data were collected using a two-part approach: (1) direct clinical assessments for anthropometrics (height, weight), blood pressure (BP), and random blood glucose (RBG); and (2) a pre-validated, structured questionnaire to document diet, physical activity, smoking, and sleep patterns. Body Mass Index (BMI) was calculated and categorized. Gender-based differences and correlations were analyzed. RESULTS: A normal BMI was observed in 59.3% of students; however, 22.1% were overweight, 8.6% obese, and 10% underweight. Hypertension prevalence was high (56.4%), while most participants had normal RBG (92.9%). Male students had significantly higher BMI, SBP, DBP, and less healthy dietary habits compared to females (P < 0.001). Positive correlations were found between BMI and both Systolic Blood Pressure (SBP) (r = 0.30) and Diastolic Blood Pressure (DBP) (r = 0.22), but not with Random Blood Glucose (RBG). High BMI was also associated with hypertension and poor sleep. CONCLUSION: Despite most students having a normal BMI, a substantial proportion exhibited elevated blood pressure, overweight, and obesity, underscoring the need for targeted lifestyle interventions and health promotion within medical education.

TI Motivation to learn artificial intelligence applications and mental
   well-being in university students: A cross-sectional study

LA English
DT Article
DE Artificial intelligence; learning; mental health; motivation; students
AB BACKGROUND:Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into higher education, while students' mental well-being has become a critical concern. The relationship between AI learning motivation and mental well-being was investigated. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cross-sectional correlational study was conducted among 195 students at the Faculty of Education, Najran University, Saudi Arabia, during the first semester of 2025-2026. Motivation significantly predicted mental well-being (beta = 0.233, R2 = 0.184, P < 0.001). CONCLUSION:Motivation to learn AI applications was positively associated with students' mental well-being and explained a modest proportion of its variance.

TI "Are nurses ready for dementia care? Insights into knowledge, attitudes,

DT Article
DE Alzheimer's; dementia; health knowledge; health personnel attitude;
   nursing
AB BACKGROUND: Dementia is a severe global health issue closely related to population aging. This study conducted to dementia-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among student nurses and staff nurses, and identified demographic and professional factors associated with these competencies. CONCLUSION: Nurses' dementia care competencies were moderate and influenced by their experience and training. TI Study protocol for effects of prone spinal decompression therapy in
   addition to Mckenzie exercises versus Mckenzie exercises only on pain
   and functional disability in lumbar radiculopathy-A randomized clinical
   trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Decompression; exercise; low back pain; pain; prone; radiculopathy
ID LOW-BACK-PAIN
AB BACKGROUND:Lumbar radiculopathy, which affects both men and women equally, are associated with symptoms of back and leg pain that significantly impairs body functioning, walking ability, and quality of life. Therefore, determining the optimal treatment protocol is necessary. The objective of the study is to evaluate the efficacy of prone spinal decompression therapy (SDT) combined with McKenzie exercises compared with McKenzie exercises alone on pain and functional disability in patients diagnosed with lumbar radiculopathy. MATERIALS AND METHODS:A single-blinded randomized clinical trial will be conducted using simple randomization at university physiotherapy department. According to sample size calculation, we aim to recruit 44 participants aged between 25 and 55 years with lumbar radiculopathy. Participants will be allocated using computer generated method and will be randomized into 2 groups: Group A (SDT + McKenzie) and Group B (McKenzie only) and each session will be lasted for 20-30 min. Outcome measures include visual analogue scale, Roland Morris disability questionnaire, Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia, Short Form-36, and patient satisfaction outcome. Global rating of change will be assessed post intervention. All outcomes measured will be evaluated at baseline, after 4 weeks (post intervention) and after week 12 (follow up). RESULTS:Based on the normality of the, parametric and nonparametric will be applied. ANOVA with Bonferroni post hoc will be used for follow-up analysis. Results will be reported with 95% confidence intervals and P values. CONCLUSION:If the findings support the combined approach, it may provide a superior conservative treatment option for lumbar radiculopathy.

   quasi-experimental study

LA English
DT Article
DE Addictive; behavior; health education; mental health; nomophobia;
   psychosocial intervention; smartphone addiction; student
AB BACKGROUND: Nomophobia, the irrational fear of being without a mobile phone or internet connection, is increasingly common among undergraduate students, contributing to psychological distress and impaired academic performance. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a psychoeducational intervention in reducing nomophobia levels in this population. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test design was employed with 217 undergraduate students. Nomophobia levels were assessed using a validated scale. The intervention, delivered in multiple sessions, focused on raising awareness about mobile dependency, its psychological effects, and coping strategies. Data were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. RESULTS: Participants were aged 17-25 years (mean 21 +/- 2.4). Instagram was the most frequently used app (46.5%). Before the intervention, 60.1% had moderate and 27.1% had severe nomophobia. Statistical analysis showed a mean negative rank of 76.74, a mean positive rank of 114.2, and a mean difference of 37.46 (Z = 7.74, P < 0.001), confirming significant improvement. CONCLUSION: The psychoeducational intervention effectively reduced nomophobia among undergraduate students. Nurse-led programs in community and hospital settings could help raise awareness and equip students with coping strategies for mobile dependency. Future studies should evaluate the long-term sustainability of these interventions and their applicability across diverse populations.

AB BACKGROUND:Providing safe and quality care is one of the fundamental principles and a primary goal in nursing. This study aimed to investigate factors related to patient safety competency among nurses working in the emergency departments of public hospitals. MATERIALS AND METHODS:This study was a correlational cross-sectional study conducted using the census method. A total of 113 nurses from the emergency departments of public hospitals in Afghanistan participated in 2023. TI How Centralized Education Systems Reproduce Inequity: A
   Multi-Stakeholder Ecological Analysis of the Real-Ideal Gap in Turkish
   Schooling
SO RESEARCH IN EDUCATIONAL ADMINISTRATION & LEADERSHIP
LA English
DT Article
DE ecological systems; theory; policy; enactment; educational; inequity;
   centralized; education systems; school leadership; multi-stakeholder
AB Large, centralized education systems frequently combine ambitious egalitarian commitments at the policy level with persistent inequities at the school level. Drawing on Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems theory, this study uses the framework diagnostically rather than cartographically to ask how that gap is produced and sustained. The empirical material consists of 32 in-depth interviews with five stakeholder categories, namely classroom teachers, school administrators, mid-level provincial and district administrators, central ministry administrators, and academic experts in educational administration, all focused on the Turkish Education System (TES). Within each ecological layer, stakeholder accounts of the system as enacted (the real) are juxtaposed with accounts of the system as desired (the ideal); the resulting layer-specific gaps are then read for shared cross-layer structure. The analysis identifies four reproduction mechanisms: decision routines that bypass stakeholder voice, a stratified teacher labor regime that geographically sorts educational quality, donation-dependent school finance that loads the financing gap onto local communities, and the hollowing of supervision into compliance audit at the expense of its developmental function. Each mechanism couples at least two ecological layers; together they explain how a centrally produced policy ambition can leave inequity intact at the school gate. The findings argue for a methodological reorientation in ecological policy research, from describing what each layer contains to diagnosing how layers couple and have implications for centralized education systems beyond the Turkish case, including those in the Middle East, the post-Soviet space, and parts of Latin America and East Asia.

TI Higher Education Leadership in the Arab World: A Systematic Review of
   Empirical Evidence
SO RESEARCH IN EDUCATIONAL ADMINISTRATION & LEADERSHIP
LA English
DT Article
DE higher education; governance; leadership; Arab; world; Gulf
ID NORTH-AFRICA; MIDDLE-EAST; EXPERIENCES; CHALLENGES; INNOVATION; ENGLISH
AB This article systematically reviews empirical evidence on higher education leadership in the Arab World. The review focused on empirical and conceptual studies published in peer-reviewed journals between 1980 and 2023. It drew on bibliographic data from Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus and followed the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Metaand data analysis. We conducted a descriptive analysis to trace the development, volume, geographic distribution, and trends of research from a broad perspective, followed by a thematic analysis of the main topical areas. The paper first presents an overall distribution, and trends, and then the main topical areas and research development, with subthemes for each. The paper concludes with theoretical and methodological reflections on current research features and recommendations for a future research agenda, policy, governance, and how leadership can better catalyze and address the immediate context and global trends in higher education development.

TI HIGHER EDUCATION AS A FACTOR OF PROFESSIONAL SUCCESS IN THE CONTEXT OF
   DIGITALIZATION: WORKING YOUTH'S EVALUATION
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA English
DT Article
DE Education; Labor Market; Labor Activity; Youth; Information Society;
   Digitalization
AB The relevance of studying education, its value and significance for work has been undeniable for decades. The purpose of the study is to analyze the assessment of young people's own education (both basic and additional) as a resource for labor activity. The study revealed that education, among the significant resources of young people, occupies a leading position, surpassing material resources, social connections and character traits, and systematic training is, in the opinion of the overwhelming majority, an indispensable component of successful work. However, in the near future, about half of the young people surveyed do not plan to receive additional education, regardless of gender. According to the study, education, as a source of new knowledge, has significant value for those young people who have clearly defined professional work goals. The authors draw conclusions about the relationship between the value of education and attitudes toward work.

TI A STUDY ON INFLUENCING FACTORS OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
   ADOPTION BY IDEOLOGICAL AND POLITICAL TEACHERS IN UNIVERSITIES
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA English
DT Article
DE Ideological and Political Education; Generative Artificial Intelligence;
   Technology Adoption
AB Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), as a key representative of the next generation of AI technology, is profoundly changing the way educational resources are supplied, knowledge production models, and teaching organization, providing new development opportunities for the digital transformation of ideological and political education in universities. University ideological and political education teachers, as the core subjects driving and realizing AI-driven educational reform, play a crucial role in the deep integration of AI and education. Given the limited focus of existing research on university teachers in my country, this study uses the UTAUT2 model to discuss the influencing factors and configuration paths of university ideological and political education teachers' willingness to use generative AI. SEM research found that performance expectations and AI literacy have the greatest impact on university teachers' willingness to use generative AI, while social influence, effort expectations, and facilitating conditions also have significant positive effects; gender, academic background, and job position have significant moderating effects on individual paths. Analysis using fs-QCA revealed five configurations of university teachers' willingness to use generative AI. Based on this, the study suggests that universities need to provide comprehensive support to teachers at multiple levels and through multiple pathways when promoting the deep integration of AI and education.

TI DEVELOPING STUDENTS' LITERARY INTERPRETATION COMPETENCE THROUGH
   SE-MIOTIC ANALYSIS OF SHAKESPEAREAN DRAMA IN LITERATURE EDUCATION
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA English
DT Article
DE Literature education; Literature Teaching Methodology; Interpretive
   Competence; Critical reading; Shakespearean Drama
AB Teaching literature in contemporary educational contexts requires strategies that move beyond the transmission of information about authors, historical periods, and plots and instead promote the development of interpretive competence and critical reading. This study examines the educational potential of literary and semiotic analysis of William Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew as a method for teaching literary interpretation. A qualitative interpretive design based on close textual reading and semiotic analysis was employed, organized through an adapted introduction, methods, results, and discussion structure. The analytical procedure examined key scenes by considering rhetorical devices, verbal irony, genre conventions, language, gesture, costume, spatial organization, and performance context. The findings show that the Christopher Sly induction enables identity to be understood as a construction based on signs and social conventions; the verbal confrontations between Katherina and Petruchio reveal language as a site of power, control, and resistance; and the taming episodes demonstrate how everyday objects and bodily representation can become mechanisms of discipline. Likewise, disguises and identity exchanges reveal the performative character of social roles, while Katherina's final speech constitutes a polysemic sign open to conservative, ironic, or subversive interpretations. The study concludes that integrating literary and semiotic analysis provides a relevant educational strategy for developing interpretive competence, critical reading, and evidence-based argumentation, enabling students to understand literary meaning as the result of the dynamic interaction among text, context, performance, and reader.

TI MULTIDIMENSIONAL EVALUATION OF THE COMPREHENSIVE POST-GRADUATE TUTORING
   MODEL: INITIAL VALIDATION AND PILOT STUDY THROUGH METHODOLOGICAL
   TRIANGULATION
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Mentoring; Postgraduate; Medical Education; Instrument Validation; Mixed
   Methods; Triangulation
AB Mentoring models in medical education have emphasized the importance of comprehensive support, yet there is limited availability of contextualized instruments that allow simultaneous assessment of their pedagogical, psychosocial, and care-research dimensions. The objective of this research was to preliminarily evaluate the Comprehensive Mentoring Model for Postgraduate Studies (MITP, by its Spanish acronym) through methodological triangulation among experts, mentees, and mentors. A mixed-methods study with a convergent design was conducted. Content validation was performed via expert judgment (n=10), a pilot study with residents and doctoral students (n=13), and semi-structured interviews with mentors (n=7). Content validity indices, Cronbach's alpha coefficient, and Kendall's W coefficient were calculated, and the sources were integrated using a qualitative convergence matrix. The 30 items of the guide obtained content validity indices above 0.78, with an S-CVI/Ave of 0.96. The scale administered to mentees showed a global alpha of 0.91. The interviews revealed four main thematic categories. Triangulation evidenced high convergence in the pedagogical and psychosocial dimensions, and partial convergence in the care-research dimension. It is concluded that the MITP shows initial favorable evidence of content validity and internal consistency. The care-research dimension emerges as a priority area for institutional improvement actions.

TI A TASK SYSTEM TO DEVELOP CRITICAL READING IN NINTH GRADERS IN COLOMBIA
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Critical reading; Literature teaching; Secondary Education; Reading
   Competence; Critical thinking
AB The teaching of literary reading in secondary education currently faces a challenge associated with fragmentary and memorization-based approaches that limit the development of critical thinking and deep comprehension of texts. In Colombia, this situation is reflected in low levels of motivation and reading competence among students, highlighting the need to rethink the didactic strategies used in the Spanish Language area. In this context, the present article aims to design and validate a task system to develop critical reading of literary works in ninth-grade students, promoting the transition from literal comprehension to critical evaluation and metacognition. The study, applied and descriptive in nature, was based on the theoretical foundations of Vygotsky's historical-cultural psychology and the didactics of the teaching-learning process. Theoretical methods (analysis-synthesis, inductive-deductive, and historical-logical) were employed, as well as the empirical expert judgment method, whose evaluation was analyzed using Kendall's coefficient of concordance (W = 0.86; p < 0.01), showing a high level of agreement regarding the system's relevance, coherence, and pedagogical feasibility. The criteria provided by the experts confirm that the sequence of twelve progressively organized tasks fosters students' reading autonomy, argumentation, and critical reflection, articulating theory and practice within a socio-constructivist approach. It is concluded that the task system constitutes an innovative and transferable proposal that strengthens the formation of critical, reflective, and culturally and socially engaged readers.

TI INSTRUMENT FOR ASSESSING STATISTICAL COMPETENCE IN PRIMARY SCHOOL
   STUDENTS IN COLOMBIA
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Statistical competence; Primary education; Educational assessment;
   Assessment instrument; Statistical reasoning
ID LITERACY
AB This article aims to design and validate an instrument for assessing statistical competence in primary school students in Colombia. The study was conducted under a descriptive approach, supported by both theoretical and empirical methods, including document analysis and expert judgment validation. The instrument consists of a contextualized pedagogical test and an analytical rubric with four performance levels, aimed at evaluating processes such as data interpretation, representation, argumentation, and decision-making. The results showed a high level of acceptance among experts regarding the relevance, clarity, and coherence of the instrument, as well as statistically significant agreement in their evaluations. Qualitative feedback highlighted its applicability in classroom settings and its potential to assess students' reasoning beyond correct or incorrect answers. It is concluded that the instrument constitutes a valid and relevant tool for assessing statistical competence in primary education, as it integrates theoretical foundations, curricular guidelines, and evaluation criteria into a coherent and contextualized proposal. Its use contributes to a broader understanding of statistical learning and provides practical support for improving assessment practices in school contexts.

TI DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND UNIVERSITY MANAGEMENT AS MEDIA-TORS IN THE
   SUSTAINABILITY OF ACCREDITATION PROCESSES
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Digital Transformation; University Management; Accreditation; Higher
   Education; Educational Quality; Sustainability
AB Digital transformation and university management have become strategic factors for the sustainability of accreditation processes in higher education. The aim of this research was to analyze the mediating role of digital transformation and university management in the sustainability of institutional accreditation processes in Ecuadorian universities. A nonexperimental crosssectional design with a quantitative approach was adopted, applying a survey to 384 administrative faculty members from six universities (three public and three private). The results show a high positive correlation (*r* = 0.883) between university institutional management and accreditation sustainability, and a regression model that explains 78 % of the variability (R-2 = 0.78). It is concluded that strengthened institutional management, based on transformational leadership, participatory governance, and innovation, is a key predictor for sustaining accreditation processes in the context of digital transformation. It is recommended to design institutional models that integrate these dimensions to ensure continuous improvement and compliance with standards.

TI IDENTIFICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED TECHNOLOGI-CAL
   COMPETENCIES DEMANDED BY TELECOMMUNICATIONS COMPA-NIES IN ECUADOR
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Artificial intelligence; Professional competencies; Telecommunication;
   Vocational training; Labour market; Technological innovation
AB The adoption of artificial intelligence in the telecommunications sector is transforming technical roles and the competencies required for entry into the labor market. This study aimed to identify and prioritize the artificial intelligence-based technological competencies that telecommunications companies consider relevant for pre-professional interns and newly hired professionals. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional, and exploratory study was conducted with 204 managers, supervisors, and area heads from companies operating in Ecuador. Data were collected through a questionnaire designed to assess competencies related to data analytics, machine learning, intelligent network operations, cybersecurity, emerging infrastructures, generative artificial intelligence, and data governance. The findings revealed a generally favorable but differentiated demand for these competencies. The strongest priorities were associated with the critical use of generative tools, data preparation and analysis, process automation, the application of artificial intelligence to network operations, and technical documentation. Competencies related to emerging technologies and highly specialized areas received comparatively lower ratings, which may reflect their level of maturity or their limited presence in entry-level professional roles. Although the instrument demonstrated adequate overall coherence, the empirical organization of the competencies did not fully reproduce the initially proposed theoretical domains. The findings suggest that university education should promote integrated learning experiences that connect artificial intelligence, data, networks, result verification, technical documentation, and responsible governance. Such an approach could help reduce the gap between academic preparation and the technological demands that students and newly qualified professionals encounter in the telecommunications workplace.

TI RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN STUDY HABITS AND ACADEMIC PERFORMAN-CE IN
   UNIVERSITY STUDENTS
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Study Habits; Academic Performance; University; Students; Study
   Techniques
AB Academic performance serves as a key indicator of student and professional success in higher education. In the context of university students in Guayaquil, study habits emerge as a determining variable of academic performance. The objective of this research was to analyze the relationship between multifactorial study habits and the self-perception of academic performance among university students in Guayaquil. A quantitative approach was adopted, utilizing a non-experimental, cross-sectional, and explanatory design. The sample consisted of 104 students selected through non-probabilistic convenience sampling. Data were collected via a structured questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4 software.The results revealed that study habits explain 63.1% of the variance in the self-perception of academic performance. The path coefficient was positive, strong, and highly significant (beta = 0,794; t = 18,454; p < 0,001). It is concluded that study habits exert a direct influence on perceived academic performance. These findings support the need to design and implement comprehensive educational programs in Ecuadorian higher education institutions that foster structured study habits, healthy lifestyles, and the proper management of psycho-social and technological factors.

TI PEDAGOGICAL INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE
   TEACHING: MODERN TOOLS AND PRACTICES
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA English
DT Article
DE AI tools; Foreign Language Teaching; Task Generation; Chatbots
AB The article examines the pedagogical potential of applying artificial intelligence (AI) tools in English language teaching within EFL and ESP programs. The study focuses on three of the most in-demand tools: chatbots for developing professional communication skills, the Twee platform for automatic task generation, and neural text-to-speech systems for creating adaptive audio materials. Findings based on classroom observations, analysis of student-produced work, and short learner surveys (B1-C1 CEFR) indicate that chatbots significantly expand opportunities for speaking practice outside the classroom, enhance fluency, develop pragmatic competence, and prepare students for professional interviews. At the same time, the need for pedagogical mediation becomes evident: instructors correct inaccuracies, monitor register, address stylistic inconsistencies, and ensure the methodological relevance of chatbot-based dialogues. The Twee platform accelerates the creation of lexical and grammatical exercises, though its automatically generated materials require refinement to improve accuracy and level alignment. The authors conclude that AI tools can substantially enrich the learning process; however, their effectiveness depends directly on the active and informed involvement of the teacher, who ensures the quality, reliability, and pedagogical relevance of all materials. AI is viewed as a supplementary resource that enhances, rather than replaces, the professional work of the instructor.

AB Continuing education within institutions is a strategic pillar for developing research skills that drive scientific innovation. TI ORGANIZATIONAL RISK MANAGEMENT AS A PREDICTOR OF ACADEMIC QUALITY IN
   MUNICIPAL EDUCATIONAL SUPPORT PROGRAMS
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Educational Organizational Risk Management; Academic Quality; Remedial
   Programs; Educational Management; Municipal Education
AB Organizational risk management in education contributes to maintaining the continuity of educational processes and supporting academic quality when educational environments face uncertainty. This study examined the relationship between organizational risk management in education and academic quality in municipal academic support programs in a canton in Ecuador. A quantitative, basic, non-experimental, descriptive-correlational, and cross-sectional design was employed. The population comprised 98 students enrolled in municipal academic support programs, who formed the sample through non-probability convenience sampling. Data were collected using a structured Likert-scale questionnaire. Internal consistency was demonstrated by Cronbach's alpha coefficients of 0.951 for organizational risk management in education and 0.968 for academic quality. Descriptive and inferential statistics were applied, including Pearson's correlation coefficient. The results indicated a very strong positive correlation between organizational risk management in education and academic quality (r = 0,882; p < 0,001) ). Significant associations were also found for academic performance, persistence and attendance, student satisfaction, and pedagogical resources and infrastructure. These findings suggest that organizational risk management in education is a strategic factor in strengthening the academic quality of municipal remedial programs, as it promotes improved learning conditions, student retention, participant satisfaction, and the efficient use of institutional resources. This study provides empirical evidence from an understudied context and establishes a foundation for educational management and public policies aimed at enhancing the resilience and quality of complementary educational programs.

TI PEDAGOGICAL CONDITIONS FOR DEVELOPING STUDENTS' EDUCATIONAL AUTONOMY IN
   HIGHER EDUCATION
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA English
DT Article
DE Educational Autonomy; Students' Educational Independence; Non-Linear
   Educational Process; Student-Centred Learning; Individual Educational
   Trajectory
AB This article examines the pedagogical conditions for developing students' educational autonomy in a non-linear educational process within Ukrainian higher education. The study is grounded in the current legal and institutional framework of Ukraine, including the principles of student-centred learning, individual educational trajectories, competence-based education, and the recognition of formal, non-formal, and informal learning. The research object is students' educational and cognitive activity, while the research subject is the system of pedagogical conditions that supports the development of educational autonomy. The study used theoretical analysis, legal analysis, pedagogical modelling, observation, questionnaires, interviews, analysis of students' written reflections, and qualitative and quantitative processing of experimental data. The diagnostic stage revealed that most students demonstrated medium or low levels of educational autonomy, especially in the diagnostic-analytical and organisational-activity-based components. The formative experiment substantiated four key pedagogical conditions: developing students' value-based motivation for educational autonomy; designing an individual educational space; implementing interactive, project-based, and digital learning technologies; and introducing pedagogical monitoring based on diagnostic, motivational-goal-oriented, activity-based, and evaluative-reflective criteria. The findings confirm that educational autonomy is not identical to independent work but represents an integrated personal and professional quality essential for lifelong learning. The results have practical relevance for improving university quality assurance mechanisms.

TI FORMATION OF TEACHERS' PSYCHOLOGICAL READINESS TO MANAGE INTERPERSO-NAL
   CONFLICTS IN THE EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT OF INSTITUTIONS
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA English
DT Article
DE Psychological Readiness; Conflict Management; School Educational
   Environment; Emotional Self-Regulation; Professional Development;
   Training-Based Learning
AB The study examines the formation of teachers' psychological readiness to manage interpersonal conflicts in the contemporary school educational environment. The research conceptualises psychological readiness as an integrative professional-personal construct comprising motivational and value-based, cognitive, emotional and self-regulatory, communicative, behavioural, and reflective components. A mixed-methods, practice-oriented research design was applied, combining theoretical analysis, observation, questionnaires, interviews, testing, expert assessment, case analysis, role-playing, video analysis, and pedagogical experimentation. The diagnostic stage involved 264 participants: 150 final-year teacher-education students and 114 early-career teachers with up to three years of professional experience. The study identifies four major configurations of interpersonal conflict in school settings: student-student, student-teacher, teacher-teacher, and teacher-parent conflicts. Four developmental levels of psychological readiness are proposed: intuitive, reproductive, constructive-adaptive, and creative-reflective. The findings emphasise that theoretical knowledge alone is insufficient for effective conflict management and should be integrated with experiential learning, emotional self-regulation, communication training, behavioural practice, and professional reflection. Particular attention is given to conflict prevention, context-sensitive professional judgement, and the distinction between ordinary interpersonal conflict and bullying, violence, discrimination, or coercion. The study substantiates the importance of interdisciplinary and training-based approaches to strengthening teachers' capacity to manage interpersonal conflicts and contribute to safe, inclusive, and psychologically supportive educational environments.

TI THE DEVELOPMENT OF COLLABORATION COMPETENCE IN HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS
   THROUGH MIND MAPPING
SO REVISTA CONRADO
LA English
DT Article
DE Collaboration Competence; Mind Mapping; High School; Students;
   Generation Alpha
AB This article examines the use of mind mapping as a pedagogical tool for developing collaboration competence among high school students (generation Alpha). The aim of the study is to identify how mind mapping correlate with the activity component of collaboration competence and to propose a model that integrates both. Primary methods include diagnostic surveys of students, structured pedagogical experimentation and assessments of created mind maps. These methods are designed to measure students' progress in key areas such as the ability to communicate effectively, adaptive communication, and reflective practice. The research resulted in two core outcomes: (1) a conceptual framework that connects the idea of a mind map (data compression, versatility, possible to create in a group) to collaboration competence components (cognitive, activity and emotional-motivational component); (2) the development and implementation of a structured system of exercises based on mind-mapping technology in foreign language instruction, which demonstrated measurable enhancements in students' ability to communicate effectively, adaptive communication skills and reflective practice. The study confirms that mind mapping can serve as an effective strategy for developing collaboration competence. The model proposed in this article can serve as a framework for similar course design in linguistic and pedagogical education.

TI Perceived Worth of Higher Education Under Scarcity: Evidence from
   Students in Guinea-Bissau
SO TRENDS IN HIGHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE student retention; higher education persistence; Guinea-Bissau; fragile
   states; campus climate; anticipatory resilience; behavioural economics
ID RESILIENCE
AB Research increasingly examines initial access to higher education (HE) in sub-Saharan Africa, yet less is known about the persistence of enrolled students in fragile contexts where costs are high and outcomes are uncertain. This study provides the first large-scale quantitative analysis of perceived HE worth in Guinea-Bissau, a resource-scarce Lusophone state. Drawing on Human Capital Investment (HCI), Behavioural Economics (BE), and Afrocentric perspectives on resilience and hope, we analysed survey data from 2255 students across six HE institutions (HEIs). A binary indicator of whether HE was worth the cost was used to assess ongoing valuation, and the data were analysed using sequential block-entry logistic regression after multiple imputation. Overall, 30.1% of students did not affirm that HE was worth the cost, indicating that enrolment does not guarantee sustained valuation. While cost-benefit reasoning remains important, perceptions were strongly shaped by campus climate and forward-looking expectations. Perceived advantages of HE, even without completion, outweighed the value of credentials alone, suggesting a pragmatic evaluation. We suggest anticipatory resilience as a lens for understanding students' sustained valuations of HE amid uncertainty, grounded in anticipated benefits, institutional experience, and relational resources. Policy should prioritise campus climate, reduce financial strain, and reinforce the intrinsic value of HE.

DT Article

ID STUDENTS
AB Smart industries base their development, maintenance, and operation on technologies compatible with what is known as Industry 4.0. In this context, the education sector needs the implementation of new learning schemes and environments for conceptual and practical learning, thereby supporting students' training to help in the industrial digital transformation. The main contributions of this work are a learning environment for robotics that integrates software applications that quantitatively measure the student's learning process; a competence framework focused on learning robotics, ROS background, and developing pickup/delivery tasks very common in the Industry 4.0 context; and a learning path implemented in step-by-step guided documentation that considers the competence framework proposed and progressively teaches ROS concepts. Then, the iBotAcademy learning environment helps to train students for the industrial digital transformation.

TI Teacher-and school-related factors associated with secondary school
   teachers' use of artificial intelligence in Spain
SO ESPIRAL-CUADERNOS DEL PROFESORADO
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence; secondary education; latent class analysis;
   technology adoption; teachers; TALIS 2024
ID ACCEPTANCE
AB Research on teachers' use of artificial intelligence in secondary education has largely relied on dichotomous classifications that obscure the internal heterogeneity of pedagogical adoption. This study identifies latent profiles of AI use in teaching and examines the teacher- and school-related factors associated with membership in each profile. Using microdata from TALIS 2024 for secondary teachers in Spain (n = 2,965; 501 schools), latent class analysis was conducted with nine dichotomous indicators of AI use, followed by R3STEP analyses with external covariates. The preferred three-class solution revealed that 68.7% of teachers did not use AI in their practice, 27.4% used it selectively, mainly for planning and content-related tasks, and 3.9% showed broad integration across multiple domains of teaching. The school-level variables examined showed no robust or consistent associations with profile membership once teacher characteristics were taken into account. The findings suggest that AI-use profile membership is more strongly associated with the perceived instructional meaningfulness of these tools than with the structural school conditions examined.

TI Development and initial validation of the Teacher-created
   (Dis)Empowering Motivational Climate Scale in Physical Education
SO ESPIRAL-CUADERNOS DEL PROFESORADO
LA English
DT Article
DE Learning environment; Teacher behavior; Achievement Goal Theory;
   Self-Determination Theory; Need-based experiences
ID QUESTIONNAIRE
AB Building on Duda's hierarchical and dimensional approach to the (dis)empowering motivational climate, this research aimed to develop and provide validity and reliability evidence for the Teacher-created (Dis)Empowering Motivational Climate Scale in Physical Education (DEMCS-PE) among Spanish secondary school students participating in Physical Education. In Study 1 (N=661; Mage = 15.06; SD = 1.34), an exploratory factor analysis and various reliability coefficients supported a 24-item, six-factor solution. In Study 2 (N=937, Mage=14.85, SD=1.32), confirmatory factor analyses psychometrically supported both a six-factor correlated model (i.e., autonomy support, task involvement, social support, control, ego involvement and coldness), and a hierarchical two-factor model (i.e., an empowering climate comprising autonomy support, task involvement and social support, and a disempowering climate consisting of control, ego involvement and coldness. Both models were invariant across gender and age. Evidence was gathered for discriminant validity, convergent validity, internal consistency and temporal stability of the instrument. Criterion validity was met through positive associations between the three dimensions and the hierarchical factor of an empowering climate with need satisfaction, and between the three dimensions and the hierarchical factor of a disempowering climate with need frustration. The DEMCS-PE is a valid and reliable measure of the students' perception of the teacher-created (dis)empowering climate in the Spanish Physical Education context.

TI Comparison of innovative and traditional methodologies in first aid
   training for college students: A quasi-experimental study
SO ESPIRAL-CUADERNOS DEL PROFESORADO
LA English
DT Article
DE Higher education; Innovative methodologies; Practical training;
   Motivation; Formative assessment
ID MOTIVATION; ENGAGEMENT
AB While traditional first aid training is teacher-centered, innovative methodology could enhance learning outcomes. Despite this, studies evaluating these innovative methods in universities are lacking. This study aims to evaluate how an innovative student-centred methodology influences motivation, first aid knowledge acquisition and consolidation, and academic performance as compared to a traditional methodology; and to analyse the relationship between the number of activities completed and grades. A quasi-experimental pretest-postest study was conducted with two groups of university students (CG: n = 43; EG: n = 44). Each entire class was assigned to one of the two study groups. Both groups received the same theoretical and practical content, differing only in the methodology. According to the primary outcomes, both groups significantly improved their acquired (p < .001 .011; eta p(2) > .08) and consolidated knowledge (p < .001; eta p(2) > .08). However, the innovative methodology increased autonomy satisfaction (p = .028; eta p(2) = .07) and reduced autonomy frustration (p = .010; eta p(2) = .09), while the traditional methodology showed a decrease in performance goal (p = .008; eta p(2) = .10), as well as an increase in mastery goal (p = .011; eta p(2) = .09) and identified regulation (p = .019; eta p(2) = .08). The number of activities carried out by EG students correlated positively with the final grade for each block (p = .044 - .050; r = .247 - .349). Both traditional and innovative methodologies are effective in improving first aid knowledge and academic performance among university students, with the innovative methodology also having a positive effect on student motivation and engagement.

TI Impact of Expanded School-Based Teaching Practices on Academic
   Engagement and Emotional Disaffection in Preservice Physical Education
   Teachers
SO ESPIRAL-CUADERNOS DEL PROFESORADO
LA English
DT Article
DE initial teacher education; physical education; academic engagement;
   teaching practice; emotional disaffection
ID UNIVERSITY-STUDENTS; SELF-CONCEPT
AB Academic self-concept and engagement are vital in teacher education, yet intervention research in authentic contexts remains scarce. This pilot study analyzed the effects of a 10-week pedagogical intervention- characterized by professional autonomy and systematic daily feedback-on academic self-concept and engagement among preservice physical education teachers (N = 28). Representing a near-census of the target population at a Spanish university facility, a quasi-experimental pre-post study with a non-equivalent control group was conducted. The experimental group participated in supervised teaching and active recess activities, while the control group followed regular university-based training. Results revealed significant improvements in academic confidence (p = .014, eta(2)(P) = .21) and emotional engagement (p = .047, eta(2)(P) = .14), as well as significant reductions in emotional disaffection (p = .002, eta(2)(P) = .30). No significant effects were found for academic effort, behavioral engagement, or behavioral disaffection (p > .05). Changes in emotional engagement explained 53.7% of the variance in emotional disaffection reductions. Expanding teaching practices through intentional support and professional responsibility primarily enhances emotional engagement and academic confidence, providing meaning and purpose to theoretical training.

TI Physically active learning through co-teaching in secondary education:
   effectiveness, implementation, and sustainability of the ACTIVA-MENTE
   program
SO ESPIRAL-CUADERNOS DEL PROFESORADO
LA English
DT Article
DE physically active lessons; teaching partnerships; teacher professional
   development; educational innovation; academic motivation
ID PERSPECTIVE
AB This study assesses the perceived effectiveness, implementation, and sustainability of the ACTIVA-MENTE program, an institutional initiative designed to integrate physically active learning in secondary education through a co-teaching model involving Physical Education teachers and teachers from other subject areas. Using an interpretive qualitative approach, we conducted semi-structured interviews and focus groups with school leadership teams, teachers, and students from 10 public secondary schools in Extremadura (Spain). Findings indicated that participants perceived physically active lessons as an effective strategy to enhance students' motivation, engagement, and emotional well-being, as well as to facilitate learning. Regarding implementation, co-teaching functioned as the driving force of the innovation, although its enactment was constrained by organizational barriers, particularly the availability of formally allocated coordination time and the distribution of responsibilities. In terms of sustainability, the program's continuity will depend on institutional integration within the school, staff stability, in-service professional development, and recognition of the working conditions necessary to prevent the model from relying on voluntarism. Overall, ACTIVA-MENTE emerges as an innovation model capable of aligning organizational structures, pedagogical action, and a collaborative culture toward a more active and healthier school.

TI Association between students' self-perceptions in physical education and
   out-of-school physical activity: the role of autonomous motivation
SO ESPIRAL-CUADERNOS DEL PROFESORADO
LA English
DT Article
DE organized exercise; unorganized exercise; motivation; self-perception;
   physical education.
ID PERCEIVED COMPETENCE; INTRINSIC MOTIVATION; EXERCISE
AB Both organized (OrPA) and unorganized physical activities (UnPA) offer known health benefits to adolescents. However, many youths are increasingly abandoning physical activity (PA). Research suggests that students' selfperceptions in physical education (PE)-such as interest, perceived competence, and the value they assign to PE- may influence PA outside of school. Yet, it remains unclear whether these factors directly impact PA or do so through other variables, like autonomous motivation. This study used a cross-sectional, mediation design framed in the Self-Determination Theory to explore whether autonomous motivation mediates the relationship between PE self-perceptions and engagement in OrPA and UnPA. A total of 1320 secondary students (average age 14.28) completed surveys measuring motivation and PA. Two mediation models were tested using R software. Perceived competence was the only significant predictor of both OrPA and UnPA. Interest, importance, and tension had no direct effects. Both models showed full mediation through autonomous motivation, particularly via integrated and identified regulations. Intrinsic motivation was not a significant mediator. Findings suggest that students' perceived competence in PE encourages out-of-school PA by enhancing motivation. PE teachers should promote self-awareness, educate on health benefits, and equip students to plan their own PA, thus fostering lasting motivation.
