TI Applying What's Learned: A Meta-Analysis on Motivation in Training
SO ESPIRAL-CUADERNOS DEL PROFESORADO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Motivation to transfer; Training transfer; PRISMA-2020; Meta-analysis
ID BIAS; RISK
AB Introduction: Despite the growing attention given to motivation to transfer as a determining factor in the process of transferring training, its exact impact is still unknown. Objective: To quantify the empirical evidence on motivation to transfer training. Methods: Meta-analysis. Searches were conducted in Web of Science, PsycInfo, ERIC and Scopus, using keywords such as 'transfer of training' or 'motivation to transfer'. Twelve studies were included. The results were limited to quantitative studies that assessed motivation to transfer using validated instruments in formal educational contexts. Publication risk was assessed using funnel plots, Egger's test, and Trim&Fill. The extracted statistics were converted to r coefficients. The effects were integrated using a random model, assessing heterogeneity, moderators, and publication bias. Results: The findings confirm that motivation to transfer is reliably associated with effective transfer, depending on the timing of training and the time elapsed until assessment. Conclusions: The evidence suggests that interventions focused on explicit transfer goals, formative feedback, and institutional support can enhance this psychological component.

TI Dialectical Materialism as an Analytic Toolkit for Critical Thinking in
   Vietnamese Higher Education: A Mixed-Methods Case Study
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE critical thinking; dialectical materialism; higher education; mixed
   methods; Vietnam
AB Dialectical materialism (DiaMat) remains a required component of Marxist-Leninist higher education in Vietnam, yet it is often taught as content to be reproduced rather than as a mode of inquiry. This bounded mixed-methods case study examined a 12-week DiaMat-infused module with 150 undergraduates at Hue University. Mean self-reported critical-thinking scores increased from 3.12 (SD = 0.54) to 3.87 (SD = 0.49), mean change = 0.75, 95% CI [0.68, 0.82], t(149) = 21.83, p < .001. Cohen's d using the pooled pre/post SD was 1.46, 95% bootstrap CI [1.28, 1.68]. Retained qualitative documentation provides selected illustrations of students using relational and threshold prompts in one translated interaction and one candidate worksheet; it does not establish prevalence, causal mechanisms, or participant-level convergence. The results therefore document change in an intervention-aligned self-report measure and limited complementary illustrations, not demonstrated critical-thinking ability or full dialectical-materialist attainment. DiaMat may have pedagogical value when enacted as a heuristic resource for inquiry rather than treated as doctrinal content.

TI The Suspension of Self-Evaluative Authority: Performativity, Audit, and
   the Politics of Recognition in Education
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE suspension of evaluative authority; recognition; performativity; audit
   culture; judgment
AB This paper argues that both teachers and students in contemporary education experience a suspension of evaluative authority: their own judgments of teaching and learning no longer count unless confirmed by external recognition. Drawing on two lived encounters - a teacher's pride unsettled by a colleague's award and a student's sense of learning displaced by overheard grades - the analysis shows how comparison structures educational life. The argument is developed through dialogue with Foucault on examination and visibility, Han on the performance society, and Agamben on suspension, alongside scholarship on performativity, audit cultures, and measurement. A brief genealogy traces how authority over self-judgment has been progressively displaced from premodern communities to modern examinations, psychometrics, and neoliberal audit regimes. The dynamics of recognition are then examined in terms of performance, delay, and conditional exemption, revealing how legitimacy is unevenly distributed yet structurally dependent on external confirmation. The paper concludes by considering the cost of this suspension and asking what it would mean for self-judgment to count once again. The analysis illuminates how performance-based accountability and audit regimes displace self-judgment upward, with implications for teacher autonomy and student agency.

AB This study examines academic staff development and employment in the context of Turkish higher education by focusing on how academic labour is experienced through staffing arrangements, promotion uncertainty, and precarious employment conditions. TI Curriculum between social justice and global standardization: A critical
   analysis of reform in primary education
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE primary education; curriculum reform; social justice; global
   standardization; performance rationality; epistemic justice; Kosovo
ID AGE
AB Curriculum reforms increasingly operate in transnational policy environments shaped by standardization, measurability, accountability, and international comparison. This article examines Kosovo's primary curriculum reform to determine how performance rationality and justice rationality are positioned within its policy architecture. The study applies qualitative critical policy analysis to the Curriculum Framework for Pre-University Education, the Core Curriculum for Preparatory Grade and Primary Education, and the Kosovo Pedagogical Institute's report on curricular overload. Coding was guided by performance rationality, Fraser's dimensions of redistribution, recognition, and representation, and epistemic justice. Alignment with European competence frameworks provides coherence and international legitimacy, but the limited specification of contextual adaptation creates a risk of epistemic dependence. The article concludes that common standards are compatible with social justice only when redistribution, participation, contextual responsiveness, and epistemic plurality are built into curriculum implementation and assessment.

TI Reconsidering the Necessity of Schooling: Castoriadian Ontology and the
   Critique of the Instituted Educational Imaginary
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE Castoriadis; imaginary; schooling; ontology; necessity
AB This article critically examines the formal representation of the school institution, drawing on Castoriadian ontology to reconsider the meaning of the value attributed to it as universally necessary and useful. In particular, it argues that this conception is neither a natural nor a purely rational construction in the context of functionalism or social constructionism, but rather a product of the instituted educational imaginary. Language plays a dual role in this process. On the one hand, its identitary dimension functions as a code, reinforcing the fixed meaning of the term "school."On the other hand, as a magma of social imaginary significations, language also reveals that schooling is not an immutable reality but rather an imaginary institution open to radical reconstruction. Referring to common arguments in favor of justifying the inherent value, and therefore compulsivity of schooling, we critically examine them through the lens of Castoriadian ontology to open up new, alternative educational forms to the accepted ones. In conclusion, this article proposes that if we understand human beings not as purely rational entities but as imaginative creators of their institutions, we can begin to dismantle the transcendent or idolatrous status of schooling. By applying Castoriadian ontology to educational theory, this paper offers a novel ontological critique of schooling's taken-for-granted necessity, revealing how language, imagination, and social creation can reconstitute the very meaning of education beyond institutional closure.

TI Mapping the Intellectual Landscape of Critical Mathematics Education: A
   Systematic Retrospective (2000-2025)
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE critical mathematics education; social justice; neoliberal critique;
   science mapping; emancipatory pedagogy
ID SOCIAL-JUSTICE; CONTENT KNOWLEDGE; EMERGING TRENDS; CULTURAL ACTION;
   SCIENCE; AUTHORSHIP; NETWORKS; STUDENTS; ISSUES; WEB
AB Critical Mathematics Education (CME) positions mathematics classrooms as sites where learners develop critical consciousness, democratic agency, and engagement with the socio-political dimensions of mathematical knowledge. CME draws on the Freirean and Frankfurt School traditions to assert that mathematics education is not a politically neutral enterprise, but a site where structures of oppression are either reproduced or contested. Despite the theoretical richness of its foundations, the intellectual structure of CME scholarship has not been comprehensively mapped. This study addresses that gap through a systematic bibliometric analysis of 160 indexed scholarly publications from 2000 to 2025, drawn from the Web of Science and Scopus databases. A science mapping approach was employed, incorporating network and temporal analyses to trace the field's conceptual evolution. The analysis is framed reflexively: citation databases are treated as commercial infrastructures whose coverage encodes linguistic and economic hierarchies that CME itself sets out to critique. Educational Studies in Mathematics emerged as the leading publication outlet, while Ole Skovsmose was the central foundational figure in the co-citation structure. Fourteen thematic groupings, read alongside timeline and time-zone visualisations, supported three broad phases: an epistemological formation phase (2000-2009), a pedagogical and teacher-oriented expansion phase (2010-2018), and a socio-political diversification phase (2019-2025) marked by climate change, decolonial perspectives, translanguaging and critical citizenship. Despite CME's dialogic commitments, collaboration networks remained fragmented. The study offers a reflexive map of the indexed CME literature and identifies both its emerging directions and the exclusions produced by the infrastructures through which that literature becomes visible.

TI Intellectual Proletariat Reification in Indonesia's Higher Education-The
   Impact of Attention Economy in Late Capitalism

AB This article examines higher education's crisis due to its declining value among younger generations within the framework of late capitalism entering the phase of neoliberalism, which also marked by the reification of intellectual proletariat in public universities in Indonesia.    Excellence in Brazil, Chile, and Peru
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE Social Justice; Education; Meritocracy; Equity; Schools
ID EDUCATION
AB This article examines how students enrolled in public high-performance excellence within highly demanding educational contexts. Drawing on focus groups with 43 students in their final year of secondary education across six approach to explore the subjectivities and tensions that shape school life in of individual effort and demanding that schools take institutional responsibility for cultivating - rather than merely attracting - excellence. Second, competition undergoes a subjective redefinition: moving away from explicit rivalry toward an internalized, emotionally mediated self-demand that students describe through situated categories such as "healthy competition," which functions as a technology of subjectivity that makes institutional pressure livable without dismantling its logic. AB The focus of the analysis highlights the social world conjured by school inspectorate quality assurance accounts ofITT contemporary provision. TI Narrative Construction in Social Studies Textbooks in Türkiye
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE ideological reproduction in education; Critical discourse analysis;
   hegemonic citizenship; national identity construction; state-citizen
   power relations
ID EDUCATION; IDENTITY
AB This study critically examines Social Studies textbooks used in Grades 4-7 in Turkey during the 2025-2026 academic year, published by the Ministry of National Education, through a critical discourse analysis framework. Drawing on critical theories of ideology, power, and hegemony, the analysis focuses on three interrelated dimensions: the discursive construction of national identity, the representation of difference and (non-)inclusivity, and the silences embedded within state-citizen relations. By interrogating the linguistic, visual, and structural organization of a sample of four textbooks, the study explores how dominant narratives function to normalize particular forms of citizenship and belonging within this corpus. The findings reveal that citizenship is constructed predominantly through an obligation-centered discourse structured around duty, loyalty, and compliance, reflecting a state-centric understanding of the citizen subject in the texts analyzed. National identity is articulated as homogeneous and exclusionary, reproduced through selective invocations of shared memory, national symbols, and heroic narratives that privilege unity over plurality. Diversity-ethnic, cultural, and religious-is incorporated in a depoliticized and folklorized manner, reducing difference to symbolic recognition while obscuring structural inequalities. Within this framework, minorities and refugees are positioned as passive, temporary, and subordinated subjects rather than as rights-bearing citizens. Furthermore, the analysis demonstrates that state-citizen relations are discursively organized through hierarchical and asymmetrical power relations, in which the state emerges as the primary agent of authority and legitimacy. Center-periphery narratives reinforce this hierarchy by constructing the center as active, rational, and normative, while marginalizing alternative voices. Given the limited sample size, these patterns should be read as indicative of tendencies within the analyzed textbooks rather than as evidence of a nationally generalized citizenship regime. By exposing the ideological work performed within this sample of Social Studies textbooks, this study contributes to critical debates on the reproduction of hegemonic citizenship discourse and calls for more inclusive, democratic, and emancipatory approaches to citizenship education.

TI Reproducing or Challenging Inequality? Ethical Dilemmas in Educational
   Decision-Making
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE Ethical dilemmas; teacher decision-making; equity in education; equity
   and justice; education policy
ID TEACHERS
AB This study critically examines how teachers and prospective teachers navigate equality-related ethical dilemmas, and how their decision-making processes may, often unintentionally, reproduce systemic inequities within educational settings. Adopting a basic qualitative research design, the research engaged participants from diverse subject areas and institutional contexts to explore how they interpret and make sense of ethical dilemmas related to equality and discrimination. Data were generated through a researcher-developed instrument that invited participants to articulate their reasoning in ethically charged scenarios and reflect on the social, cultural, and institutional factors shaping those choices. Content analysis revealed that prospective teachers tended to prioritize support for students perceived as disadvantaged, whereas teachers more frequently invoked legal compliance and institutional regulation as moral anchors. These findings highlight persistent ethical tensions between equity, professional responsibility, and accountability, underscoring the need for ethically and critically informed teacher education and professional development that foreground reflexivity and social justice in educational practice.

TI Pro-poor tourism as ideology: A critical pedagogical analysis of
   poverty, participation, and neoliberal subject formation
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE Pro-poor tourism; neoliberalism; ideology; participation; tourism;
   critical tourism education
AB Pro-poor tourism (PPT) emerged as an approach aimed at increasing the economic benefits of tourism for poor people and contributing to poverty reduction. The approach particularly emphasizes income, employment, economic participation, and entrepreneurship as ways of enabling poor people to benefit more from tourism. However, how PPT defines poverty, what understanding of development it legitimizes, and how it positions poor people require a more critical examination., This conceptual study reconsiders PPT from a critical pedagogical perspective. Drawing on Freirean critical pedagogy Marxist Critical Policy Analysis, and critiques of neoliberalism, it discusses how PPT constructs meanings of poverty and participation and how it relates to particular forms of subject formation. The analysis draws attention to the tendency of PPT to approach poverty less as a structural and political problem and more as a problem that can be addressed through economic participation. Within this framework, poor people can be positioned as entrepreneurial subjects expected to develop their economic capacities within existing market relations. The study distinguishes economic participation from a form of critical participation that questions and seeks to transform existing social relations, and argues that PPT should be considered not only in terms of its economic outcomes but also in terms of the meanings it produces, the relations it legitimizes, and the forms of subjectivity it promotes. From this perspective, the implications for tourism education point to the need to move beyond employability and adaptation to market needs and to create learning processes through which students can critically question poverty, inequality, power, and ideology.

AB Designing a writing model that integrates culture and critical thinking is an important factor in achieving communicative competence and multicultural awareness. TI Student Perceptions of Obstacles in Science Careers are Not Altered by
   Scientist Stories of Challenges
SO CBE-LIFE SCIENCES EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
ID MIDDLE-SCHOOL STUDENTS; ROLE-MODELS; ACADEMIC-PERFORMANCE; CONTEXTUAL
   SUPPORTS; BARRIERS; GENDER; MOTIVATION; CLASSROOM; FAILURE; IMPACT
AB Incorporating counterstereotypical scientist role models into undergraduate biology courses is a powerful, evidence-based way to support student persistence in STEM fields. However, educational resources featuring counterstereotypical scientists could unintentionally have adverse impacts on student attitudes towards science. Here, we leveraged a multi-institution experiment that manipulated whether educational materials included information on the obstacles faced by counterstereotypical scientists in their careers. After students received these variable materials, we documented the obstacles they perceived they may face as scientists. Through the lens of attribution theory, we found that students are aware of a variety of obstacles they would face as scientists and that student perceptions of those obstacles are not changed by sharing the obstacles that scientists had to overcome. We encourage instructors to share scientists' stories of the obstacles they faced in their careers without concern that this will alter students' perceptions of careers in science.

TI An Exploratory Study of Teachers' Perceptions of School Administrators'
   Affiliative Humor, Organizational Support, and Well-Being
SO PSICOLOGIA EDUCATIVA
LA English
DT Article
DE Teachers; School administrators; Affiliative humor; Perceived
   organizational support; Mental well-being
ID JOB-SATISFACTION; MENTAL-HEALTH; LEADER HUMOR; MEDIATING ROLE; WORKING
   HOURS; BURNOUT; COMMITMENT; SUPERVISOR; HAPPINESS; VALIDITY
AB This study aimed to reveal the relationship between teachers' perceptions of school administrators' affiliative humor use and teachers' mental well-being by focusing on the mediating role of perceived organizational support (POS). A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 542 teachers working in public primary schools located in Antalya, Turkey, using three measures: affiliative humor, perceived organizational support, and mental well-being. Mediation testing was performed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapping procedures. The findings of the study revealed that teachers' perceptions of school administrators' affiliative humor use were positively related to teachers' mental well-being and POS. Furthermore, teachers' POS was found to be positively related to their mental well-being. The results further suggested that POS was associated with the relationship between teachers' perceptions of administrators' affiliative humor and teachers' mental well-being, indicating a partial mediating role within the examined model. Consequently, our results emphasize that when teachers perceive higher levels of affiliative humor by their school administrators, they tend to report higher levels of perceived organizational support (POS), and this perception is associated with higher levels of teachers' mental well-being.

TI Issues and Approaches to Gifted Education in Specialist Music Programs
   Globally: Insights From Institutional Leaders
SO GIFTED EDUCATION INTERNATIONAL
LA English
DT Article
DE care ethics; conservatories; gifted children; giftedness and talent;
   musically gifted; pre-college education; professional leadership;
   specialist music education
ID CONCEPTIONS; TEACHERS
AB Globally, a range of specialized talent development music programs offer training for young musically gifted children to develop their musical abilities to an advanced, professional level of performance. In recent years, various constituencies have reported on significant shortcomings in some of these programs, sparking intense debates concerning the necessity of continuing what they view as overly specialized talent development programs. Presently, there has been no comprehensive and systematic overview of the current situation for gifted children in specialist music education. This qualitative, collective case study examines the current challenges identified by 81 leaders overseeing 68 specialized music programs in 25 countries. Findings reveal a wide array of critical issues and approaches to specialized music education for gifted children that range from a focus on serving the children to a focus on children serving the system. The study emphasizes how diverse stakeholders can recognize gifted children as individuals, and not just as potential musicians who benefit others.

TI Gamification, Popular Musics-Based Repertoire, and Mixed Instrumentation
   in Music Enrichment: A Case Study With Gifted Learners in Spain
SO GIFTED EDUCATION INTERNATIONAL
LA English
DT Article
DE high intellectual abilities; gamification; music education; popular
   musics-based repertoire; creativity; collaboration
AB This study examines a gamified musical enrichment program using mixed instrumentation and a popular musics-based repertoire with students identified as having high intellectual abilities (HIA) in Spain. Forty-six participants (ages 9-16, M = 12.4) attended six Saturday sessions in Primary (n = 24) and Secondary (n = 22). Conducted in C & aacute;ceres, Extremadura, within the TalentiaCC program, the extracurricular setting enabled activities designed to encourage participation, creativity, and engagement in a culturally relevant framework. Data included observation, narrative records, audiovisual materials, and teacher reflections. Collaboration was fostered by scaffolded roles, and creativity appeared through rhythmic-timbral variations (Primary) and improvisations with harmonic modifications (Secondary). Five design principles emerged-scaffolded roles, short narrative, moderated collaboration, adaptable repertoire, clear criteria-offering guidance for inclusive music programs and teacher education.

TI When Black Students Speak: Testimony, Anti-Blackness, and the Psychic
   Commons
SO HARVARD EDUCATIONAL REVIEW
LA English
DT Article
DE Afropessimism; anti-Blackness; Black students; education; public
   opinion; racism
ID EDUCATION; BIAS
AB In this article, Lauren Wells examines how Black students' accounts of anti-Black racism are recast as they move from school board testimony into broader public conver-sation. Drawing on Afropessimism and the concept of the psychic commons, she analyzes public meeting testimony and thirty-nine news articles spanning four critical incidents in a midsize urban district. TI Change in Early Disability Identification Rates since COVID-19: Location
   Matters
SO AUSTRALASIAN JOURNAL OF EARLY CHILDHOOD
LA English
DT Article
DE community resources; early disability identification; geographic
   inequity
ID SOCIAL DETERMINANTS; HEALTH; PEOPLE; CHILDREN
AB Access to early intervention services for children with disabilities depends on early identification efforts. Utilizing the Bioecological Theory of Human Development, which underscores the complex interplay between child development, historical context/time, and several systems, this study examined changes in early disability identification rates within one U.S. state pre- and post-COVID-19 (2015 and 2021; 132 counties) and whether community resources helped contextualize shifts. The weighted average relative change of disability identification rate increased by 19.15% (M = 129.61, range = -204.28-5,497.30), though unequal across counties and cities. Community factors, including population size, minoritized population, and urbanicity, were associated with rate changes. Higher-resourced communities had greater increases in identification rates. Varying investment levels across communities contributed to unequal access to vital developmental resources. Findings inform how we understand the nuanced needs of communities for more strategically-informed policy decisions.

TI Influence of Maternal Employment on the Self-Esteem of Adolescents: A
   Comparative Study
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Family Environment; Gender Norms; Psychosocial Development; Role
   Modelling; Self-concept
AB Mothers' participation in the workforce is a significant social and economic phenomenon that influences family functioning and adolescent development. This study examines the impact of maternal employment on adolescent self-esteem, with particular attention to gender differences. Using an exploratory research design, data were collected from 201 adolescents (104 with working mothers and 97 with non-working mothers) from the Jorhat district of Assam, employing the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale. The findings reveal that adolescents of working mothers demonstrate significantly higher self-esteem than those of non-working mothers, likely due to greater independence, exposure to role models, and enhanced social interactions. Additionally, male adolescents of working mothers reported higher self-esteem than female adolescents, while no significant gender differences were observed among adolescents of non-working mothers. These results suggest that societal expectations and gender norms may shape self-esteem development differently. The study highlights the important role of maternal employment in fostering adolescent self-confidence and underscores the need for supportive interventions to promote positive self-esteem among adolescents regardless of maternal work status.

TI Faculty and Students' Perception about Gender-Responsive Pedagogy in
   Isabela State University, Philippines
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Curriculum Development; Educational Inclusion; Equity Awareness;
   Instructional Strategies; Teacher Preparedness; Workplace Diversity
AB Gender-responsive education is essential to advancing inclusive and equitable higher education. This study examined faculty engagement in gender-sensitive teaching at Isabela State University and identified inputs for strengthening its gender-responsive pedagogy framework. An explanatory mixed-methods design was employed involving 270 faculty members and 1,841 students during the second semester of Academic Year 2023-2024. Quantitative data were collected using an adapted Gender-Sensitivity Teaching Test and analysed using descriptive statistics and independent-samples t-tests, while qualitative responses were analysed thematically. Both faculty members and students reported very frequent engagement in gender-sensitive teaching practices, with gender equality receiving the highest ratings. Significant differences were observed across several indicators of teaching practices and gender equality. Qualitative findings revealed inconsistencies in language use, tensions between personal beliefs and professional responsibilities, gaps between awareness and practice, challenges in promoting participation, and social-emotional demands. The findings highlight the need for sustained professional development, curriculum integration, systematic feedback, and institutional mechanisms to strengthen consistent, equitable, and gender-responsive pedagogy across university classrooms.

TI Perception of Coaches and Students Towards Sports Safety Risk Management
   Practices in Secondary Schools in Philippines
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Emergency Preparedness; Injury Prevention; Risk Assessment; Safety
   Management; Sports Safety
ID INJURY; PREVENTION
AB Sports safety is essential to protecting student-athletes and maintaining effective school sports programs. This study examined sports safety risk management practices in three large secondary schools near Isabela State University-Echague Campus and provided inputs to enhance sports safety in schools. A quantitative descriptive-comparative research design was employed, involving a purposive sample of 30 coaches and 150 student-athletes. Data were collected using a sports safety risk management questionnaire and analysed using means, standard deviations, and independent-samples t-tests. Coaching and supervision emerged as the strongest dimension, whereas training and preparation, as well as equipment and facilities, showed notable weaknesses. No significant differences were found between coaches' and student-athletes' perceptions of sports safety risk management practices. Risk assessment and prevention received the lowest ratings, while health and medical support emerged as the strongest area. The findings highlight the need for continuous safety education, systematic risk assessment, emergency preparedness, regular facility maintenance, strengthened medical support, policy enforcement, and institutional monitoring to promote safer school sports environments.

TI Predictive Validity of a Diagnostic Mathematics Assessment on Freshmen
   Calculus Performance in Engineering Programs in a Polytechnic College in
   Philippines
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Math Readiness; Engineering Education; Academic Result; Entry Test;
   College Testing
AB This study emphasises early academic support and performance monitoring in engineering education. It examined the predictive validity of a diagnostic mathematics assessment on Calculus performance among first-year engineering students at Camarines Sur Polytechnic Colleges. It investigated whether scores in Algebra, Trigonometry, Solid Geometry and Analytic Geometry could predict academic outcomes in Calculus. A correlational design was employed, using data from 787 purposively selected students enrolled in the 2022-2023 academic year. The findings a affirm the value of diagnostic assessments in identifying students at risk and informing early intervention strategies in engineering education.

AB In secondary education, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is quickly changing the teaching and learning practices. TI Skills Limitations, Resource Constraints and Workload Pressure as
   Barriers in Conducting Research among Public Elementary School Teachers
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Capacity Building; Educational Leadership; Innovation; Organisational
   Support; Professional Development
AB Despite increasing expectations for teacher-led research, public elementary school teachers continue to encounter persistent challenges that hinder their ability to initiate, conduct, and complete research activities effectively. This qualitative research utilised a structured open-ended question to gather the data from the 62 elementary school teachers using thematic analysis with inductive coding for data processing. Three emerging themes were identified in the study based on the responses of teachers with regard to their research writing experiences, which include capacity and skills limitations, resource and support constraints and workload pressures. The emergence of these themes provides empirical evidence that human capital development among public elementary school teachers is constrained by the combined influence of individual competencies, institutional support systems, and organisational demands, thereby extending existing literature on teacher professional development in basic education.

TI Exploring Teachers' Practice of Technology Use in Blended Teaching: A
   Qualitative Inquiry
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Instructional Design; Pedagogical Innovation; Professional Development;
   Reflective Practice; Technology Utilisation
ID INTEGRATION
AB This qualitative study investigates how 14 faculty members recruited via purposive sampling integrate technology within a blended learning context at Cagayan State University-Aparri, utilising the SAMR model as an analytical framework. Semi-structured interview data were analysed using Braun and Clarke's (2006) thematic analysis. Findings revealed that technology utilisation spans a developmental spectrum from instructional enhancement to pedagogical transformation. In lesson presentation, faculty advanced beyond tool substitution, leveraging multimodal platforms and blended classroom architectures to achieve augmentation and modification. In facilitating discourse, the strategic use of synchronous collaborative workspaces shifted practices into modification and redefinition by establishing an elastic instructional loop. Finally, in evaluation, the deployment of gamified platforms and real-time diagnostic visualisations modified traditional testing paradigms into dynamic feedback loops, while automated analytics pushed practices toward redefinition. Collectively, the findings demonstrate that technology has matured from an ad hoc additive into a structural element that fosters transformative, student-centred learning.

TI Quality in postgraduate research: The influence of interconnected
   elements

LA English
DT Article
DE student; topic; supervision; institution; community; interconnected
   elements
ID DOCTORAL SUPERVISION; CHALLENGES; TRANSITION
AB Quality in postgraduate research is a socially constructed concept that undergoes regular reinterpretation and adaptation. Debates raise questions concerning the factors that influence the student's achievement of all the attributes associated with the concepts of mastery and doctorateness. TI Centring well-being as an indicator of quality in the
   internationalisation of higher education
SO SOUTH AFRICAN JOURNAL OF HIGHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE African international students; internationalisation of higher
   education; quality; wellbeing
ID STUDENTS; EXPERIENCES; CHALLENGES
AB Over the past decade, student mobility within Africa has increased significantly, with South Africa emerging as a key destination for students from across the continent. This shift challenges traditional understandings of internationalisation, which have predominantly focused on South-North mobility, and calls for greater attention to the quality of internationalisation in African higher education. While universities increasingly pursue internationalisation strategies, less attention has been paid to what constitutes quality internationalisation from the perspective of those who experience it. Drawing on a qualitative study of staff and African international students at two South African universities between 2021 and 2022, this paper examines students' experiences. The findings show that institutional approaches to quality remain centred on academic provision and mobility, while limited attention is given to international students' well-being, sense of belonging, administrative experiences, and access to institutional support. We argue that quality internationalisation should be understood as more than the successful implementation of mobility initiatives or the achievement of institutional performance indicators. Rather, it should be evaluated in terms of the extent to which universities foster the well-being, belonging, and flourishing of both international students and staff. Positioning well-being as a central indicator of quality offers a more holistic and human-centred understanding of internationalisation in African higher education.

AB The transformation of Higher Education (HE) in South Africa has emerged as an urgent national priority, driven by persistent concerns regarding the quality, equity, relevance, and sustainability of the sector. Therefore, this position paper provides a blend of the author's perspectives and the extant literature on the purpose, quality, and sustainability of HE in South Africa; the challenges militating against its quality and sustainability; strategies for its sustenance; and the prospects thereof. This reflective paper, underpinned by the Fitness of Purpose Theory, provides viable strategies and prospects for achieving HE quality and sustainability in South Africa. It concludes that HE is the lifeline of nations and economies, and calls for a cohesive, diversified Higher Education ecosystem that prioritises student access, success, and social impact.

TI Quality tutoring practices in higher education: The role of writing
   centres in supporting postgraduate students in South Africa
SO SOUTH AFRICAN JOURNAL OF HIGHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE writing centre; tutors; postgraduate students; training; academic
   writing support; higher education
ID CONSULTANTS; SPACES; TALK
AB Writing centres are integral in the promotion of quality tutoring practices that address the varied and evolving writing needs of students in higher education. As postgraduate writers navigate complex academic and research expectations, university writing centres serve as key spaces for developing academic writing competence and confidence. Ensuring quality tutoring in these spaces requires a deep understanding of postgraduate students' writing needs and systematic training for tutors who provide this support. Drawing on Humanising Pedagogy and Communities of Practice, this study examines how writing centres foster quality tutoring that empowers postgraduate writers. Anchored within an interpretivist qualitative framework, this study the writing centre's role in in supporting postgraduate students and examined how quality tutoring practices are cultivated through targeted tutor development. Data was generated through a focus group discussion with fourteen writing centre tutors, ten interviews with postgraduate students, as well as six interviews with writing centre practitioners at two Universities of Technology (UoTs) in South Africa. Using thematic analysis, supported by NVivo 15, the findings highlight that while tutors possess strong foundational knowledge, many feel underprepared for the specialised demands of postgraduate academic writing. This underscores the need for continuous professional training, institutional integration of writing centre support, and the promotion of empathetic, collaborative tutoring approaches. This study concludes that quality tutoring is characterised by confident, reflective, and adaptive tutors who engage postgraduate writers as partners in the learning process. Most writing centre research centres on undergraduate writers; thus, this article fills this gap by specifically focusing on postgraduate writers' needs and tutor preparedness for that level. By investing in tutor training and institutional collaboration, writing centres can enhance postgraduate writing success and overall academic quality in South African higher education.

   professionalisation of academics as university teachers

LA English
DT Article
DE higher education; quality education; university teachers; quality
   teaching; professionalisation
ID STUDENTS; SUCCESS
AB Academics, as university teachers, are crucial role players in quality higher education provision. This article firstly argues that, as shown in higher education literature, many of them enter the academy as subject-matter experts without being equipped with the necessary pedagogical competencies, which has implication for the quality of education provision. TI Perspectives on community engagement from institutional audits: A weak
   link in the higher education quality chain
SO SOUTH AFRICAN JOURNAL OF HIGHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE quality; community engagement; institutional audits; transformation;
   decoloniality
AB Learning and teaching, research, and community engagement are considered central to the purpose and mandates of higher education institutions. The study adopted a qualitative documentary analysis in which 26 Council on Higher Education (CHE) institutional audit reports from the 2022-2024 cycle were reviewed to explore the meaning and emphasis given to community engagement (CE) in the CHE institutional documents. The findings revealed that while CE is articulated in institutional rhetoric, visions, and missions, there is little tangible evidence of its implementation in institutional actions. The main issues include the absence of formal coordination structures, limited dedicated funding, minimal integration into core academic activities such as curriculum and research, and reliance on individual champions rather than institutional support. Additionally, the findings highlight the significant impact of the absence of monitoring and evaluation systems that measure developmental outcomes. Grounded in Community Development Theory and Decoloniality, the study shows that as a part of higher education, CE should not be marginalised if the sector aims for transformation and social justice. Against that background, the findings indicate that to secure transformative social justice objectives, CE must be systemically embedded in institutional structures and mechanisms of governance, funding and quality assurance. The study, therefore, recommends that CE, as a fundamental part of academic achievement, requires concerted institutional and national efforts and intentional leadership.

TI Ubuntu as a framework for quality in doctoral programmes
SO SOUTH AFRICAN JOURNAL OF HIGHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Ubuntu; doctoral students; quality assurance; parents; doctoral
   education
ID EDUCATION
AB The systemic pressure within South African higher education to accelerate doctoral production risks favouring throughput over substance. This strain remains unaddressed by standard quality assurance (QA) frameworks, which tend to promote a rushed approach, narrowly focusing on quantifiable outcomes such as short completion times and independent research, while neglecting the psychosocial and holistic aspects of students' lives. This paper argues that current QA standards largely adopt a Western-based "I think, therefore I am" orientation, placing a disproportionate emphasis on cognitive mastery, while downplaying the need to foster the holistic development of researchers whose knowledge and impact are deeply rooted in their social context. The study proposes that, to counter this, QA frameworks must integrate an Ubuntu-based "I am because you are" orientation if they are to recognise the critical influence of students' social roles, responsibilities, and relationships as essential levers, and to infuse the transformation envisaged in the democratic dispensation into doctoral QA. Drawing on in-depth interviews with 19 past and present doctoral students who are parents and mostly employed, the study undertakes a discourse analysis to examine how their social roles and responsibilities shape their experience of quality learning, highlighting the essential dimensions of community engagement and situated knowledge that are currently neglected by existing QA models. The findings reveal a systemic quality trap arising from a mismatch between rigid institutional metrics and students' lived realities, based on four themes: conflicting paradigms that penalise relational responsibilities; institutional cultural myopia regarding necessary support structures such as childcare; a cumulative burden resulting from intersecting identities; and a constriction of student agency.

   Being; academic pipeline; decolonisation; precarity

Recommendations are made that universities take seriously the call to decolonise if they wish to address the leaky academic pipeline.

TI The role of quality management systems in enhancing online education: A
   case study of a business school in KwaZulu-Natal
SO SOUTH AFRICAN JOURNAL OF HIGHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Online education; quality management systems; higher education;
   technology; infrastructure
AB The shift to online education created opportunities for innovation while raising questions about the effectiveness of existing quality assurance (QA) systems. This study evaluated the Quality Management System (QMS) of an online learning programme at a Business School in KwaZuluNatal (KZN). A mixed-methods approach was used, combining surveys of students and interviews with academic experts in quality management and higher education. Ninety-six students participated in the survey and eleven academics participated in the interviews. Findings from the survey revealed key challenges such as limited internet access, high data costs, and cybersecurity risks, which negatively affected student engagement and equitable access to learning. Despite these challenges, the students reported overall satisfaction with the programme, particularly with lecturer support. The interview data highlighted the need for structured QA frameworks to maintain academic standards in online education. A gap analysis at the business school showed institutional strengths such as a clear mission and commitment to continuous improvement, but also weaknesses, notably the absence of a dedicated QMS framework tailored to online education. The study proposes a QMS framework based on the ISO 21001:2018 standard and supported by Total Quality Management (TQM) principles. The framework incorporates continuous improvement mechanisms, regular assessments, and feedback systems to strengthen quality assurance and support the sustainability of online programmes.

TI Digital technologies and artificial intelligence: A catalyst for the
   transformation of traditional work-integrated assessment in higher
   education
SO SOUTH AFRICAN JOURNAL OF HIGHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Work-integrated learning; virtual work-integrated assessment; artificial
   intelligence; digital technologies; transformation
AB Traditionally, assessment of work-integrated learning (WIL) is conducted face-to-face, with the assessor physically in the same place as students to evaluate their acquisition of professional knowledge, skills, and competencies. However, the rapid technological advancements, changing workplace practices, and disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the need for more flexible and innovative assessment strategies. Virtual WIL assessment (VWA), which leverages digital technologies, artificial intelligent tools, and virtual simulations, arose out of this need. In the discourses on VWIL, some scholars have theorised about the transformative potential of digital technologies and AI to enhance flexibility, access, collaboration, and reflective practice without explicitly demonstrating how this phenomenon occurs or has occurred. This study investigated the potential of digital technologies and AI tools to transform traditional WIL assessment (TWA) in higher education. The research question was "How can digital technologies and AI tools contribute to the transformation of TWA? The objective was to (i) explore digital technologies and AI tools employed to virtually assess WIL and (ii) to examine how these strategies can transform TWA. Guided by the interpretivist paradigm and underpinned by transformative learning theory, the study adopted a qualitative case study design. Semi-structured open-ended interviews were used to collect data from 15 purposively selected participants and analysed using colour-coding to identify emergent themes. The rationale for the study stemmed from the growing demand for technology and AI-enabled assessment practices that are compatible with the changing world of work. Results revealed that these tools can foster empowerment, autonomy, and independence and unleash innovation and creativity while enhancing meaningful engagements. The study concludes that these tools have a significant potential to transform TWA by expanding opportunities for authentic, inclusive, and sustainable assessment in higher education. It is recommended that universities invest in digital infrastructure, develop capacity, and integrate virtual assessment models into WIL policies to promote student employability and meet the demands of the twenty first century and the fourth industrial revolution.

DE professional integration; professional identity of teachers; Bachelor's

AB Introduction. TI Creativity as a resource for educational management: barriers and
   facilitators across professional groups
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE barriers; creativity; development; facilitating factors; flexibility;
   managers; students; university faculty
ID ENVIRONMENTS; BRAIN; MODEL
AB Background Creativity represents a crucial psychological resource that supports adaptive performance and professional growth in dynamically changing environments. Despite its recognized importance, comparative analyses of creativity across different occupational groups remain limited.Methods The present study examines variations in creativity levels among three professional categories-students, university faculty, and managers-representing different stages of professional development. A comparative quantitative design was employed to assess creativity indicators, including flexibility, originality, curiosity, and risk-taking.Results The findings revealed that students demonstrated the highest overall creativity levels, followed by university faculty, whereas managers exhibited the lowest. Group differences were explained by the dynamic interaction of contextual barriers and facilitators. For students, creativity was stimulated by self-expression and intrinsic motivation but hindered by fear of mistakes and conformity pressure. Faculty members benefited from academic autonomy and intellectual challenge, yet faced constraints due to administrative load and conservative institutional culture. Managers experienced the strongest inhibiting factors, such as risk avoidance and rigid thinking, although supportive leadership and self-confidence served as facilitating resources.Conclusion These results highlight the contextual and developmental determinants of creative potential and emphasize the need for targeted interventions to strengthen creativity-fostering environments within educational and organizational systems. The study contributes to a more nuanced understanding of creativity as a resource for effective educational management and leadership development.

TI Primary English as a foreign language learners' reception of a
   subtitling activity based on an artificial intelligence-generated
   «anime»
SO TECNOLOGIA CIENCIA Y EDUCACION
LA English
DT Article
DE language learning; artificial intelligence (AI); educational technology;
   subtitling; grammar competence; pedagogical translation; English as a
   foreign language (EFL); primary education
ID AUDIOVISUAL TRANSLATION
AB This exploratory study investigates the reception and perceived usefulness of a subtitling activity based on an artificial intelligence (AI)-generated & laquo;anime & raquo; video in the context of English as a foreign language (EFL) learning in four fifth-grade primary EFL classrooms in two Spanish state schools in Spain. A short original anime episode was created using generative AI tools, with a narrative designed to provide contextualised practice of key grammatical structures previously addressed in class, namely the verb to be, have got, frequency adverbs, and the present continuous. A total of 72 pupils aged 10-11 watched the video and completed an individual subtitling translation task using the free SubpandaTM tool. They were provided with an SRT (SubRip subtitle) template in English and were asked to translate each segment into Spanish. Afterwards, all participants completed a short questionnaire consisting of the & laquo;Smileyometer & raquo;, & laquo;Again-Again & raquo;, and one item on perceived usefulness for grammar learning, while a subsample of six voluntary learners took part in a focus group. Results revealed high levels of enjoyment, engagement, and willingness to repeat the activity. Learners also reported that the activity was helpful for understanding grammar in context and for reflecting on language use. Overall, this study offers a preliminary proposal for integrating AI-generated narrative media and pedagogical translation into Primary EFL subtitling tasks.

TI Assessing oral production in French using multimodal artificial
   intelligence with Google AI Studio in secondary education
SO TECNOLOGIA CIENCIA Y EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence (AI); language instruction; oral expression;
   French as a foreign language (FFL); formative assessment; psychological
   effects; secondary education; educational innovation
AB The development of oral expression in foreign languages is often hindered by communicative anxiety and a lack of immediate feedback. This study examines the impact of multimodal artificial intelligence, using Google AI Studio, as a formative assessment tool in the learning of French as a foreign language (FLE). Using a quasi-experimental design in secondary education (n = 48), rubrics, observation scales, and questionnaires were employed to measure outcomes. The findings show that the use of this educational innovation not only improved phonetic accuracy and fluency but also generated positive psychological effects by reducing the affective filter. The tool's & laquo;algorithmic privacy & raquo; enhances student agency and voluntary iteration, demonstrating that AI acts as an emotional scaffold in language teaching. As a conclusion, transforming error into technical data fosters the autonomy and resilience necessary for success in digital contexts.

TI Gamified digital resources in the teaching of grammar in English for
   specific purposes: university students' perspectives
SO TECNOLOGIA CIENCIA Y EDUCACION
LA English
DT Article
DE gamification; English for specific purposes (ESP); English grammar;
   educational tech nology; student perception; higher education;
   motivation
AB This article examines the use of gamified digital resources in the teaching of grammar within English for specific purposes (ESP) to undergraduate students enrolled in a Tourism degree, with particular attention to students'perceptions of the methodological experience developed over the course of a semester. To this end, a quantitative approach was adopted through a pre-experimental single-group design. The sample consisted of 87 first-year students. Data were collected through an initial and a final perception questionnaire, an initial diagnostic grammar test, a final achievement test, and the scores obtained in activities carried out with Genially, Educaplay, Quizizz, Edpuzzle, and Nearpod. The data were analysed by means of statistical descriptive and inferential procedures. The results show an overall positive assessment of the use of these resources, particularly in the dimensions related to teaching style, perceived learning, and motivation. Likewise, the dimension concerning anxiety and self-efficacy in relation to new digital resources revealed a more heterogeneous experience. With regard to achievement, no statistically significant differences were found between the initial and the final grammar test, although higher overall performance in the digital activities was associated with a relatively more favourable development. It is concluded that gamified digital resources can enrich the methodological experience and foster a more positive disposition towards grammar learning in ESP contexts, although this does not necessarily entail a significant improvement in overall achievement.

TI Artificial intelligence mediated learning of Chinese grammar: usage,
   perceptions, and reliability among university students
SO TECNOLOGIA CIENCIA Y EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence (AI) in language learning; Chinese grammar;
   pedagogical mediation; sociocultural theory; critical agency;
   algorithmic reliability; generative language models; DeepSeek; ChatGPT
AB This study examines the mediation of artificial intelligence (AI) in the learning of Chinese grammar by Spanish-speaking university students (n = 26), combining an analysis of their AI-assisted grammatical analysis tasks (scripts) with their self-reported perceptions through a questionnaire. Based on a mixed-methods design, the research analyzed 19 AI-assisted scripts and the responses to a 23-item questionnaire (including Likert scales, multiple-choice questions, and open-ended items), with the aim of exploring grammatical accuracy, learners'critical agency (that is, their ability to autonomously evaluate, question, and verify the responses generated by AI), and the perceived reliability of two models (ChatGPT and DeepSeek). Findings reveal a pedagogical paradox: although students display a strong critical stance toward AI, such awareness does not consistently translate into an effective detection of grammatical errors. Results also show a predominantly static use of the tool, which limits its dialogic potential as a mediator within the zone of proximal development. The comparison between models among those who used both systems indicates a clear preference for DeepSeek in terms of perceived accuracy and usefulness, highlighting the importance of training corpora for typologically distant languages. Overall, AI emerges as a complementary form of scaffolding that requires teacher mediation to ensure rigorous learning and to prevent the uncritical adoption of algorithmic errors.

TI Emerging technologies and language studies. Integration of generative
   artificial intelligence into teaching
SO TECNOLOGIA CIENCIA Y EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE educational project; higher education; teacher digital competence (TDC);
   language subjects; teaching innovation; teaching experiences; generative
   artificial intelligence (AI)
AB This paper describes the development of a teaching innovation project at the Universidad Autonoma de Madrid (Spain) over the course of two academic years. Led by a group of lecturers from various teaching disciplines, all of which are language-related (language in use, applied linguistics, language teaching, natural language processing and translation), the project covered a wide range of educational levels (graduate and postgraduate), courses and subjects (core modules, compulsory modules and optional modules). The general purpose was to explore the educational applications of generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems to develop teaching materials for different linguistic uses. The project also involved integrating these tools into students' didactic tasks. In the first stage of the project, the focus was on the teacher, and in the second stage, on the student. The results obtained signal these two different dimensions, because, on the one hand, it probes necessary to train teachers to improve their digital competence (TDC), and on the other hand it is necessary to provide students with basic training on the ethical use of generative AI in academic contexts, as a large percentage of them use this technology without any prior training.

TI Evaluation of mobile apps for music education: an analysis of
   perceptions from university students
SO TECNOLOGIA CIENCIA Y EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE information and communication technologies (ICT); mobile apps; music
   education; app evaluation; perceptions; students; smartphones
ID INTERVENTION
AB The incorporation of information and communication technologies (ICT) in education has significantly transformed the teaching-learning processes. This study focuses on evaluating mobile apps for music education, analyzing the perceptions of university students. A quantitative, descriptive and cross-sectional design was adopted. The sample consisted of 180 students from the bachelor's degree programs in Primary Education and double degree in Primary Education and Early Childhood Education. The data was collected through a 70-item questionnaire, evaluating technical, pedagogical and musical aspects of the apps. These data were analyzed using the SPSS V.29 program. The results indicated a high reliability of the assessment instrument (Cronbach's alpha of 0.950) and a high consistency in the average measures (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] of 0.950). The evaluated apps showed a high technical and aesthetic quality, as well as in the musical aspects, although the pedagogical-functional dimension obtained a slightly lower score. Apps that facilitate exercise and playful learning predominated, but a low frequency of evaluation functions was identified. In conclusion, mobile apps have great potential to enrich music education, providing interactive and accessible tools that can improve both teaching and learning. However, it is necessary to improve certain pedagogical and functional aspects to maximize its educational impact.

TI Training in information and communication technologies for future
   Paraguayan teachers and its implementation during their practicums
SO TECNOLOGIA CIENCIA Y EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE information and communication technologies (ICT); trainer of trainers;
   initial teacher education; professional practice; digital education;
   professional development in teaching; digital competence
AB In the current educational context, a paradigm that integrates information and communication technologies (ICT) at all levels is required, emphasizing teacher training as a fundamental pillar for thriving in virtual and personalized environments. In Paraguay, since 2019, a transformation process in teacher education has been underway, prioritizing innovation and ICT proficiency to address the needs identified by educational stakeholders. This research aims to evaluate the teacher training curriculum regarding the inclusion of ICT, the training experiences during the educational process, and its application in professional practice, identifying strengths and weaknesses from the perspective of those who have gone through this process. The study was qualitative-quantitative, descriptive and crosssectional. The curriculum subjects were analyzed considering competencies, content, methodology, and assessment. Additionally, self-assessment questionnaires were administered to 200 students and graduates (men and women) of the Basic Education Teacher Training Program for the first and second cycles, exploring their knowledge, use, application, and ICT-related skills both during training and in professional practice. The findings reveal a discrepancy between the integration of ICT into the curriculum and the current demands for innovative educators. Participants reported having basic knowledge of ICT, obtained mostly through parallel training at the Instituto de Formaci & oacute;n Docente (IFD), and they recognize these tools as essential for implementing active methodologies and personalized teaching strategies. This study highlights the urgent need to strengthen teacher education curricula in ICT to ensure that educators can meet the demands of contemporary education.

TI A mobile app proposal for the safe movement of young people with
   disabilities through the urban environment
SO TECNOLOGIA CIENCIA Y EDUCACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE disability; youth; accessibility; displacement; urban environment;
   barriers; mobile application
AB Accessibility aims to ensure that all people can access spaces, information, and services on an equal basis. However, people with disabilities face multiple barriers that hinder their social inclusion, such as physical, communication, political, programmatic, health, and transportation obstacles, among others. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 15% of the world's population has some form of disability, highlighting the importance of eliminating these barriers. This project aimed to map the most frequently used routes by people with disabilities in the city of C & oacute;rdoba and improve their accessibility. For this research, the Cicerone mobile application was designed, allowing users to record the barriers they encounter on their daily commutes. This study employed a participatory methodology, involving people with disabilities in the design and testing of the application. Furthermore, collaboration between experts and users enabled the development of accessible routes based on artificial intelligence (AI). The project emphasizes the importance of technology and an interdisciplinary approach to improving accessibility and promoting the autonomy of people with disabilities.

TI How Blended Work-integrated Learning Fosters Students' Creative Design
   Competencies
SO ELECTRONIC JOURNAL OF E-LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Blended learning; Work-integrated learning; Boundary crossing; Creative
   design education; e -Learning
AB Grounded in boundary crossing theory, we developed and examined a Blended Work-Integrated Learning (B-WIL) framework. Guided by an action research design, this study implemented the model in an undergraduate toy design course characterised by a blended ecology, dual-scale mentorship, and student-centred education. Operating as a critical "boundary broker," the local mentor translated high-level global insights into the material realities of physical practice. 28 group reflection reports were collected and analysed through a dual-track qualitative strategy: (1) deductive process tracing of design episodes and (2) inductive thematic analysis of perceived competency development. Findings suggest that students encountered recurring challenges, including contextual dissonance, interpretive disconnects, prototype failures, and design fixation, yet resolved them through evolving patterns of support-seeking, experimentation, and cross-boundary communication. The local broker emerged as a key figure in mediating cultural misunderstandings, reframing global critiques, and validating physical prototypes that remote experts could not directly assess. Across the two project cycles, students demonstrated a marked behavioural shift: from epistemic dependence on expert authority towards autonomous, peerdriven experimentation and earlier engagement with material prototyping. The thematic analysis points to three emergent trans-boundary competencies cultivated through the B-WIL environment: sociomaterial fluency, contextual agility, and cross-boundary communication. These competencies equip students to navigate the digital-physical divide, reconcile local cultural identity with global market expectations, and synthesise complex knowledge across spatial and disciplinary boundaries. The study concludes that the B-WIL framework reframes the disembodiment risk of virtual WIL as productive boundary friction that accelerates professional growth. It also offers an actionable, scalable blueprint for institutions seeking to integrate global virtual networks with local physical mentorship, helping students remain materially grounded while becoming globally fluent.

TI Digital Inequality and e-Learning Barriers for Incarcerated Students in
   UNISA Correctional Hubs
SO ELECTRONIC JOURNAL OF E-LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Cognitive barriers; Correctional education; Learning centre access; DCS
   oversight; Digital literacy; Incarcerated students
ID EDUCATION
AB Open distance e-learning (ODeL) has broadened access to higher education for marginalised groups worldwide. However, for incarcerated students, correctional environments impose restrictions on internet access, communication, and study time that undermine the flexibility central to ODeL. In South Africa, the University of South Africa (UNISA) operates elearning hubs in partnership with the Department of Correctional Services (DCS). Despite this initiative, limited empirical evidence exists on the study experiences of incarcerated students, particularly regarding cognitive and contextual barriers. This study investigates (i) the cognitive and learning barriers faced by incarcerated distance students (RQ1) and (ii) the ways their experiences differ from those of non-incarcerated students (RQ2). A quantitative survey of 45 students across three UNISA hubs (Kgo & scaron;i Mampuru II and Brandvlei Correctional Centres) was conducted using anonymous paper questionnaires to protect respondent anonymity. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, with results reported as headcount frequencies due to the small sample size. Findings reveal significant structural constraints. 58% of respondents reported insufficient access time, with internet use restricted to weekday mornings and middays, and no evening or weekend access. The importance of this finding lies not only in the quantity of available time but in the fragmentation and unpredictability of access. ODeL systems assume continuity of engagement, whereas correctional access structures interrupt study routines and reduce students' ability to regulate their own learning. Nearly half engaged with the online library for less than one hour daily, while 62% received little or no librarian support. Peer collaboration was limited, with 40% unable to participate in online forums, and DCS oversight further constrained autonomy, with 58% requiring daily approval for educational activities. 87% enrolled with UNISA for the first time after incarceration, meaning that the correctional hub was their initial point of contact with tertiary e-learning. These results demonstrate a mismatch between ODeL requirements and correctional conditions. Recommendations include extending hub access hours, strengthening library and digital literacy support, improving academic responsiveness, and enabling supervised collaboration mechanisms compatible with security requirements. By providing empirical evidence from South Africa, this study advances understanding of correctional elearning. It contributes to international debates on digital inclusion in correctional education and informs policy interventions aimed at promoting educational equity for incarcerated students. The findings also highlight the importance of aligning institutional support structures with pedagogical needs, ensuring that incarcerated students are not disadvantaged compared to their non-incarcerated Peers.

TI Fostering Nursing Faculty Well-Being: Developing the Pilot Trinitas
   Mentorship Model to Support a Healthy Academic Culture
SO NURSING EDUCATION PERSPECTIVES
LA English
DT Article
DE Caring Science; Work-Life Balance; Nurse Faculty Mentorship;
   Organizational Culture; Recruitment and Retention
AB This pilot study used Charmaz's constructivist grounded theory and Watson's theory of human caring to develop the Trinitas Mentorship Model with 11 new nurse faculty. Data from 10 monthly focus groups and pre-/post-questionnaires were analyzed. ID ANXIETY
AB Nurse anesthesia students face high rates of burnout, anxiety, and depression that can impair learning and clinical readiness. Between jun and November 2024, a university nurse anesthesia program implemented trauma-informed wellness initiatives, including flexible scheduling (condensed on-campus days, excused absences, virtual attendance for distant sites), a pass/fail reflective wellness assignment, regular cohort town halls, weekly community emails, a final-year professional course with mindfulness/provider-wellness content, and a program-specific career fair. Following implementation, first-time national certification examination pass rates rose from 83 percent (2023) to 91 percent (2025). A trauma-informed, multilevel wellness approach was associated with improved program outcomes.

SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English

   performance-based funding; sustainable development financing; university

AB The expansion of HEIs in Uzbekistan has generated a new finance problem: universities must expand access, develop research capacity and modernise infrastructure with still-constrained public budgets. This paper presents a policy-oriented model relating financial autonomy to sustainable development funding of HEIs during Uzbekistan's shift from cost-based to rating-linked performance funding. TI Understanding the dynamics of physical education: a qualitative study of
   its roles and challenges in Pakistan
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE curriculum implementation; health and fitness; Pakistan; physical
   education; secondary school
ID HEALTH; PERSPECTIVE; SATURATION; INTERVIEWS; SCHOOLS; IMPACT; PLAY
AB Purpose Physical education (PE) at the secondary school level is indispensable for endorsing the physical health, mental wellbeing, and social development of students. It supports overall development while nurturing teamwork, discipline, and resilience among students. Despite its importance, research on the roles and challenges of PE in Pakistan is limited. Based on Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems theory, this qualitative study investigates the roles and challenges of physical education at the secondary school level in Pakistan.Methods The study used phenomenological qualitative research design to examine the roles and challenges of physical education at the secondary school level. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 10 PE teachers working at the secondary school in Pakistan. The interview data were analyzed using manual thematic analysis, generating three main themes: (1) health perspectives, (2) facilities and resources, and (3) curriculum implementation.Results The findings indicate that PE significantly impacts the students' mental and physical health and enhances teamwork and leadership qualities. However, challenges such as a shortage of trained PE teachers, inadequate facilities for physical activities, and insufficient government funding support limit the effectiveness of the PE program. These demonstrates that the effectiveness of PE is influenced not only by classroom-level practices but also by broader institutional and policy environments.Implications The findings highlight the need for greater government investment in PE resources, curriculum integration, and trained PE teachers to establish an effective and comprehensive PE program at the secondary school level. Strengthening this interconnected school, institutional, and policy condition is essential for establishing a more inclusion, effective, and comprehensive PE program in Pakistani secondary schools.

TI Motivation, engagement, and autonomy in gamified mobile-assisted
   language learning: undergraduate EFL learners' perspectives
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE English as a foreign language (EFL); gamification; learner autonomy;
   learner engagement; mobile-assisted language learning (MALL); Saudi EFL
   context
ID USER ACCEPTANCE; DIGITAL GAME; GAMIFICATION; DEVICES
AB This mixed-methods study investigates Saudi undergraduate English as a foreign language (EFL) learners' perceptions of gamified mobile-assisted language learning (MALL) and its relationship with motivation, engagement, autonomy, confidence, social interaction, and perceived effectiveness. A structured questionnaire was administered to 175 undergraduate students, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with a purposive subsample of 12 female participants. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, while qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis following an established qualitative approach, with interview findings used to explain and illuminate the quantitative patterns. Findings reveal consistently high levels of positive perception across both dimensions, with learners attributing their motivation and engagement primarily to rewards, competition, and progress tracking, and their autonomy and confidence to the flexibility and immediate feedback afforded by mobile applications. Thematic analysis yielded six themes, including enhanced enjoyment and novelty, competitive engagement, reward-driven motivation, improved attention, contextual flexibility, and minor technical challenges. The study contributes to digital education research by providing empirical, theoretically grounded evidence from a gender-segregated Saudi higher education context, and by adopting a multidimensional mixed-methods framework that captures both the strength and the experiential texture of learners' engagement with gamified MALL. Implications are discussed for the pedagogically meaningful integration of gamified mobile applications in university-level EFL instruction.
